objects.description: A final concrete ILogHandler implementation that writes log messages to the console. It supports an option to include the source location in output and uses a mutex to serialize console writes. It is non-copyable via Uncopyable. Construction is via the public constructor or the static Create() factory returning a shared_ptr to ILogHandler.

objects.definition:
namespace opendnp3
{

class DNP3ManagerImpl;

/**
 *	Root DNP3 object used to create channels and sessions.
 */
class DNP3Manager
{

public:
    /**
     *	Construct a manager
     *
     *	@param concurrencyHint How many threads to allocate in the thread pool
     *	@param handler Callback interface for log messages
     *	@param onThreadStart Action to run when a thread pool thread starts
     *	@param onThreadExit Action to run just before a thread pool thread exits
     */
    DNP3Manager(uint32_t concurrencyHint,
                std::shared_ptr<opendnp3::ILogHandler> handler = std::shared_ptr<opendnp3::ILogHandler>(),
                std::function<void(uint32_t)> onThreadStart = [](uint32_t) {},
                std::function<void(uint32_t)> onThreadExit = [](uint32_t) {});

    ~DNP3Manager();

    /**
     * Permanently shutdown the manager and all sub-objects that have been created. Stop
     * the thead pool.
     */
    void Shutdown();

    /**
     * Add a persistent TCP client channel. Automatically attempts to reconnect.
     *
     * @param id Alias that will be used for logging purposes with this channel
     * @param levels Bitfield that describes the logging level for this channel and associated sessions
     * @param retry Retry parameters for failed channels
     * @param hosts List of host addresses to use to connect to the remote outstation (i.e. 127.0.0.1 or www.google.com)
     * @param local adapter address on which to attempt the connection (use 0.0.0.0 for all adapters)
     * @param listener optional callback interface (can be nullptr) for info about the running channel
     * @return shared_ptr to a channel interface
     */
    std::shared_ptr<IChannel> AddTCPClient(const std::string& id,
                                           const opendnp3::LogLevels& levels,
                                           const ChannelRetry& retry,
                                           const std::vector<IPEndpoint>& hosts,
                                           const std::string& local,
                                           std::shared_ptr<IChannelListener> listener);

    /**
     * Add a persistent TCP server channel. Only accepts a single connection at a time.
     *
     * @param id Alias that will be used for logging purposes with this channel
     * @param levels Bitfield that describes the logging level for this channel and associated sessions
     * @param mode Describes how new connections are treated when another session already exists
     * @param endpoint Network adapter to listen on (i.e. 127.0.0.1 or 0.0.0.0) and port
     * @param listener optional callback interface (can be nullptr) for info about the running channel
     * @throw DNP3Error if the manager was already shutdown or if the server could not be binded properly
     * @return shared_ptr to a channel interface
     */
    std::shared_ptr<IChannel> AddTCPServer(const std::string& id,
                                           const opendnp3::LogLevels& levels,
                                           ServerAcceptMode mode,
                                           const IPEndpoint& endpoint,
                                           std::shared_ptr<IChannelListener> listener);

    /**
     * Add a persistent UDP channel.
     *
     * @param id Alias that will be used for logging purposes with this channel
     * @param levels Bitfield that describes the logging level for this channel and associated sessions
     * @param retry Retry parameters for failed channels
     * @param localEndpoint Local endpoint from which datagrams will be received
     * @param remoteEndpoint Remote endpoint where datagrams will be sent to
     * @param listener optional callback interface (can be nullptr) for info about the running channel
     * @throw DNP3Error if the manager was already shutdown
     * @return shared_ptr to a channel interface
     */
    std::shared_ptr<IChannel> AddUDPChannel(const std::string& id,
                                            const opendnp3::LogLevels& levels,
                                            const ChannelRetry& retry,
                                            const IPEndpoint& localEndpoint,
                                            const IPEndpoint& remoteEndpoint,
                                            std::shared_ptr<IChannelListener> listener);

    /**
     * Add a persistent serial channel
     *
     * @param id Alias that will be used for logging purposes with this channel
     * @param levels Bitfield that describes the logging level for this channel and associated sessions
     * @param retry Retry parameters for failed channels
     * @param settings settings object that fully parameterizes the serial port
     * @param listener optional callback interface (can be nullptr) for info about the running channel
     * @throw DNP3Error if the manager was already shutdown
     * @return shared_ptr to a channel interface
     */
    std::shared_ptr<IChannel> AddSerial(const std::string& id,
                                        const opendnp3::LogLevels& levels,
                                        const ChannelRetry& retry,
                                        SerialSettings settings,
                                        std::shared_ptr<IChannelListener> listener);

    /**
     * Add a TLS client channel
     *
     * @throw std::system_error Throws underlying ASIO exception of TLS configuration is invalid
     *
     * @param id Alias that will be used for logging purposes with this channel
     * @param levels Bitfield that describes the logging level for this channel and associated sessions
     * @param retry Retry parameters for failed channels
     * @param hosts IP address of remote outstation (i.e. 127.0.0.1 or www.google.com)
     * @param local adapter address on which to attempt the connection (use 0.0.0.0 for all adapters)
     * @param config TLS configuration information
     * @param listener optional callback interface (can be nullptr) for info about the running channel
     * @throw DNP3Error if the manager was already shutdown or if the library was compiled without TLS support
     * @return shared_ptr to a channel interface
     */
    std::shared_ptr<IChannel> AddTLSClient(const std::string& id,
                                           const opendnp3::LogLevels& levels,
                                           const ChannelRetry& retry,
                                           const std::vector<IPEndpoint>& hosts,
                                           const std::string& local,
                                           const TLSConfig& config,
                                           std::shared_ptr<IChannelListener> listener);

    /**
     * Add a TLS server channel
     *
     * @throw std::system_error Throws underlying ASIO exception of TLS configuration is invalid
     *
     * @param id Alias that will be used for logging purposes with this channel
     * @param levels Bitfield that describes the logging level for this channel and associated sessions
     * @param mode Describes how new connections are treated when another session already exists
     * @param endpoint Network adapter to listen on (i.e. 127.0.0.1 or 0.0.0.0) and port
     * @param config TLS configuration information
     * @param listener optional callback interface (can be nullptr) for info about the running channel
     * @throw DNP3Error if the manager was already shutdown, if the library was compiled without TLS support
     *                  or if the server could not be binded properly
     * @return shared_ptr to a channel interface
     */
    std::shared_ptr<IChannel> AddTLSServer(const std::string& id,
                                           const opendnp3::LogLevels& levels,
                                           ServerAcceptMode mode,
                                           const IPEndpoint& endpoint,
                                           const TLSConfig& config,
                                           std::shared_ptr<IChannelListener> listener);

    /**
     * Create a TCP listener that will be used to accept incoming connections
     * @throw DNP3Error if the manager was already shutdown or if the server could not be binded properly
     */
    std::shared_ptr<IListener> CreateListener(std::string loggerid,
                                              const opendnp3::LogLevels& loglevel,
                                              const IPEndpoint& endpoint,
                                              const std::shared_ptr<IListenCallbacks>& callbacks);

    /**
     * Create a TLS listener that will be used to accept incoming connections
     * @throw DNP3Error if the manager was already shutdown, if the library was compiled without TLS support
     *                  or if the server could not be binded properly
     */
    std::shared_ptr<IListener> CreateListener(std::string loggerid,
                                              const opendnp3::LogLevels& loglevel,
                                              const IPEndpoint& endpoint,
                                              const TLSConfig& config,
                                              const std::shared_ptr<IListenCallbacks>& callbacks);

private:
    std::unique_ptr<DNP3ManagerImpl> impl;
};

} // namespace opendnp3
objects.description: Root manager class that owns the DNP3 thread pool and provides factory methods to create channels (TCP/UDP/Serial/TLS) and listeners. It encapsulates internal implementation via a pimpl (DNP3ManagerImpl). Construction starts worker threads; Shutdown stops them and tears down sub-objects. Exact threading and lifetime semantics beyond this are not documented here.
Strongly-typed enumeration of library error conditions used by the opendnp3 API. Values include SHUTTING_DOWN, NO_TLS_SUPPORT, and UNABLE_TO_BIND_SERVER.
Utility struct that provides a static to_string(Error) function mapping Error values to human-readable messages. It is not intended to be instantiated; it has no data members.

Final exception class derived from std::runtime_error used to throw opendnp3-specific errors. It formats its message from an Error via ErrorSpec::to_string, optionally appending a std::error_code message.

Abstract interface representing a shutdown-capable resource. Classes deriving from IResource must implement Shutdown() to release or stop the resource. The virtual destructor allows safe deletion via the interface pointer.

Abstract interface in the opendnp3 namespace representing a protocol stack (master or outstation). It inherits from IResource and exposes synchronous control of communications (Enable/Disable) and a method to retrieve StackStatistics. No implementation details are provided here; concrete stacks implement this interface.
Referenced base class for IStack, declared in opendnp3/IResource.h. Not defined in this header; therefore excluded per instructions.
Referenced return type from opendnp3/StackStatistics.h. Not defined in this header; therefore excluded per instructions.

Root statistics struct aggregating DNP3 link- and transport-layer counters for a master or outstation session. Provides nested types for Link and Transport, and owns instances of each as fields. Default-constructible and constructible from Link and Transport values.
Nested struct holding link-layer error/counter metrics for a session: unexpected frames, bad master bit, unknown destination/source. Used as a field inside StackStatistics.
Nested struct grouping transport-layer counters and composing nested Rx and Tx structs. Default-constructible and constructible from Rx and Tx. Owned by StackStatistics.
Nested struct of Transport counters for receive-side transport protocol data units: valid, error, overflow, discard, ignore. Owned by Transport.
Nested struct of Transport counters for transmit-side transport protocol data units. Owned by Transport.

Concrete value-type class representing an analog command event in DNP3 (Group 43). It holds the commanded analog value, the command status, and an optional event time. Provides default and value/status(/time) constructors and equality comparison. Ownership is by value; no special destruction semantics are indicated. Details of CommandStatus and DNPTime are defined elsewhere.

Concrete analog output type carrying a 16-bit signed integer value. Serialization corresponds to DNP3 Group 41, Variation 2. Declares constructors and equality operator; method bodies are not defined in this header.

Concrete analog output type carrying a 32-bit signed integer value. Serialization corresponds to DNP3 Group 41, Variation 1. Declares constructors and equality operator; method bodies are not defined here.

Concrete analog output type carrying a 32-bit IEEE-754 float value. Serialization corresponds to DNP3 Group 41, Variation 3. Declares constructors and equality operator; method bodies are not defined here.

Concrete analog output type carrying a 64-bit IEEE-754 double value. Serialization corresponds to DNP3 Group 41, Variation 3. Declares constructors and equality operator; method bodies are not defined here.
Referenced enumeration for command result status. It is included from opendnp3/gen/CommandStatus.h and not defined in this header; details unknown here.

Abstract base class for DNP3 measurements holding quality flags and timestamp. It provides protected constructors and two public data members: flags (quality) and time (timestamp). Intended to be a base for concrete measurement types. No virtual destructor or methods are defined; lifetime management is by value or through derived types.

A DNP3 application-layer event type representing a binary output command event (maps to group 13 variations 1/2). It stores the commanded boolean value, the DNP3 command status, and an optional DNP timestamp. Multiple constructors allow building from Flags, from explicit value/status, and with/without time. GetFlags() encodes value/status into Flags using internal bit masks; equality compares all fields. Exact serialization rules are not shown here; details must be derived from implementation. Ownership is not specified; this is a standalone value type.

A small value-type class representing a bitmask of DNP3 point/event classes (subset of classes 0–3). It encapsulates a uint8_t bitfield with helper constructors from PointClass, EventClass, a raw mask, or booleans, plus query/mutation helpers (HasClassN, Set/Clear, Intersects, OnlyEventClasses). Details of EventClass and PointClass enums are external to this header. Lifetime is trivial; no special construction/destruction semantics beyond standard C++ object usage.

Concrete class representing a DNP3 Control Relay Output Block (CROB) request. It bundles the operation type, trip/close code, timing parameters for pulse operations, repeat count, a raw control code byte (for non-standard codes), and the resulting/desired command status. Provides constructors to create from structured fields or a raw code, equality helpers, and a QU flag test derived from rawCode. Details about memory management are standard value semantics; no special destruction required.
direct_api_constructors: opendnp3::ControlRelayOutputBlock::ControlRelayOutputBlock(OperationType, TripCloseCode, bool, uint8_t, uint32_t, uint32_t, CommandStatus)

objects.description: A simple timestamp structure representing a DNP3 time value and its associated TimestampQuality. Provides constructors for default (invalid) time, synchronized time from a uint64 value, or explicit value+quality, and an equality operator comparing both fields.
A trivial placeholder struct used when an event type does not require any metadata. It contains no fields or behavior.

objects.definition:
enum class EventType : uint16_t
{
    Binary = 0,
    Analog = 1,
    Counter = 2,
    FrozenCounter = 3,
    DoubleBitBinary = 4,
    BinaryOutputStatus = 5,
    AnalogOutputStatus = 6,
    OctetString = 7
};
objects.description: Strongly-typed enumeration (backed by uint16_t) identifying the DNP3 event type/category (e.g., Binary, Analog, Counter). Used to discriminate event measurements in the opendnp3 stack. No constructors or ownership semantics apply to enums.

Strongly-typed enumeration (backed by uint8_t) representing DNP3 event classes (Class 1/2/3). Used to classify event priorities or reporting categories. No constructors or ownership semantics apply to enums.

Lightweight bitfield wrapper used to represent DNP3 measurement quality/status flags. Holds a raw uint8_t and provides typed helpers to set/test bits corresponding to various Quality enums (BinaryQuality, DoubleBitBinaryQuality, AnalogQuality, CounterQuality, FrozenCounterQuality, BinaryOutputStatusQuality, AnalogOutputStatusQuality). No ownership semantics; trivially constructible and copyable.

A POD struct in the opendnp3 namespace representing a DNP3 group/variation identifier pair as two uint8_t fields. Default-constructs to 0xFF/0xFF (often indicating 'unknown' or 'unset'). Provides a value constructor for explicit group and variation. No special ownership or lifetime semantics; trivially copyable.

namespace opendnp3
{

enum class IINBit
{
    BROADCAST = 0,
    CLASS1_EVENTS,
    CLASS2_EVENTS,
    CLASS3_EVENTS,
    NEED_TIME,
    LOCAL_CONTROL,
    DEVICE_TROUBLE,
    DEVICE_RESTART,
    FUNC_NOT_SUPPORTED,
    OBJECT_UNKNOWN,
    PARAM_ERROR,
    EVENT_BUFFER_OVERFLOW,
    ALREADY_EXECUTING,
    CONFIG_CORRUPT,
    RESERVED1,
    RESERVED2 = 15
};

} // namespace opendnp3
objects.description: Strongly-typed enumeration of the DNP3 IIN (Internal Indications) bit positions spanning the two-byte field. Values 0–7 map to the LSB and 8–15 to the MSB. Provides semantic names for individual indication bits such as event classes, time needed, device trouble, and various request error flags.

A concrete two-byte DNP3 Internal Indications (IIN) field container with bitwise utilities. Holds LSB and MSB bytes and provides methods to set/clear/test bits by IINBit, combine fields (|, |=, &, &=, ~), clear all bits, and query for request errors. Note: declarations for IsSet, SetBit, ClearBit, SetBitToValue, and operator== are provided here; their definitions are expected in the corresponding source file. Thread-safety is not implied; users should guard concurrent access. The static REQUEST_ERROR_MASK is declared but defined elsewhere.

Traits/metadata struct for Binary measurements. Provides associated measurement type, value type, default event/static variations, and type enums. Inherits privately from StaticOnly to prevent instantiation (utility holder only). Construction details are unknown; it contains only typedefs and static constants.
Traits/metadata struct for DoubleBitBinary measurements, tying the measurement class and value enumeration to event/static variations and enums. Non-instantiable via StaticOnly.
Traits/metadata for BinaryOutputStatus measurements. Maps to value type and default event/static variations. Non-instantiable (StaticOnly).
Traits/metadata for Analog measurements with double value type. Provides associated event/static variations and enums. Non-instantiable (StaticOnly).
Traits/metadata for Counter measurements using 32-bit unsigned values. Supplies default event/static variations and type enums. Non-instantiable (StaticOnly).
Traits/metadata for FrozenCounter measurements with 32-bit unsigned values. Associates event/static variations and enums. Non-instantiable (StaticOnly).
Traits/metadata for AnalogOutputStatus measurements. Links to double value type and provides default event/static variations and enums. Non-instantiable (StaticOnly).
Traits/metadata for OctetString measurements. Provides default event/static variations and enums. No value_t alias (payload is OctetString). Non-instantiable (StaticOnly).
Traits/metadata for TimeAndInterval measurements. Provides the static variation and type mask. No event variations. Non-instantiable (StaticOnly).

Represents a boolean measurement (on/off) with DNP3 Flags and optional timestamp via the TypedMeasurement<bool> base. Constructors allow creating from value, flags, and time. Full behavior and fields are inherited from TypedMeasurement<bool> (not defined here).

Double-bit binary measurement with four-state DoubleBit value, quality flags, and optional timestamp. Provides helpers to map between packed Flags and DoubleBit using bit masks. Inherits storage/fields from TypedMeasurement<DoubleBit>.
Represents the current state of a binary control output as a measurement with flags and optional time. Rarely used in practice. Inherits implementation details from TypedMeasurement<bool>.
Analog measurement (double) with quality flags and optional timestamp via TypedMeasurement<double>.
Monotonic non-negative counter measurement (uint32_t) with flags and optional timestamp via TypedMeasurement<uint32_t>.
Snapshot of a Counter taken at a freeze instant, represented as uint32_t with flags and optional timestamp via TypedMeasurement<uint32_t>.
Reports the last set value of an analog output as a measurement (double) with flags and optional timestamp via TypedMeasurement<double>.

Composite value mapping to DNP3 Group50Var4 containing a timestamp, an interval duration, and a units field (as raw uint8_t) with helper to obtain typed IntervalUnits. Primarily used in the DNP3 Profile for periodic variations (PV).

A small value-type class in namespace opendnp3 representing an octet string (bitstring) of up to 255 bytes. It stores data internally in a fixed-size std::array<uint8_t, 255> and tracks the active length. It provides constructors from default, C strings, and a Buffer view, plus Set methods and a ToBuffer view accessor. Details like memory ownership and bounds are handled internally. Destruction is trivial; no heap ownership is implied.

A small wrapper class in namespace opendnp3 representing DNP3 group 110/111 octet string objects. It derives from OctetData (defined elsewhere) and provides three constructors that delegate to the base: a default that yields a single 0x00 byte, one from a C string (length determined by strlen, null terminator not copied, truncated to 255 bytes), and one from a Buffer read-only slice (also truncated to 255, defaulting to [0x00] if empty). Destruction/ownership follow normal C++ semantics; no additional members are declared here.

Configuration class for retry behavior of an opendnp3 channel. It stores minimum/maximum open retry intervals and an optional reconnect delay, and delegates backoff calculation to an IOpenDelayStrategy (default is exponential backoff). Provides a static Default() factory and a NextDelay() helper that computes the next retry delay bounded by maxOpenRetry. Construction requires TimeDuration parameters and a strategy reference; destruction semantics are trivial (no ownership of the strategy). Details of TimeDuration, IOpenDelayStrategy, and ExponentialBackoffStrategy are defined elsewhere and not part of this header.

Abstract interface representing a communication channel that can host one or more DNP3 master or outstation stacks. Provides synchronous retrieval of link-layer statistics, control of log filter levels, and factory methods to create and bind master or outstation sessions to the channel. Lifetime is managed externally; destruction is virtual. Derived implementations must implement all pure virtual methods. Ownership/management semantics for created stacks are via std::shared_ptr returned by AddMaster/AddOutstation.

Abstract callback interface used to observe state transitions of a running DNP3 channel. Implementers override OnStateChange to receive ChannelState updates. No concrete construction is provided here; users supply their own implementation and pass instances to APIs that accept an IChannelListener.

Abstract interface in the opendnp3 namespace representing a running TCP/TLS listener that can be shut down to stop accepting new connections. It derives from IResource (declared in opendnp3/IResource.h), inheriting resource lifecycle operations. Only a virtual destructor is defined here; concrete implementations are provided elsewhere.

Abstract interface that defines a policy for computing the next open/retry delay for a connection given the current delay and a maximum bound. Intended to be implemented by strategies such as exponential backoff.

Concrete, singleton implementation of IOpenDelayStrategy that computes delays using an exponential backoff algorithm. Non-copyable via Uncopyable. Access is provided via Instance(); GetNextDelay returns the next delay clamped by max. Exact backoff formula is not shown in this header.

Lightweight value type representing an IP endpoint (IPv4 address string and TCP/UDP port) in the opendnp3 namespace. Provides convenience constructors for binding to all adapters (0.0.0.0) or localhost (127.0.0.1). The type owns the address string and the port value; it is trivially copyable/movable as a struct with standard members. No explicit destruction logic beyond default semantics.

Concrete final implementation of IChannelListener that writes channel state changes to std::cout. Non-copyable via private inheritance from Uncopyable. Provides a static factory method returning a shared_ptr<IChannelListener>.

A configuration struct in opendnp3 providing serial port parameters and sensible defaults (9600 8N1, no flow control, 500 ms async open delay). Fields include device name, baud rate, data bits, stop bits, parity, flow control, and an asynchronous open delay. Constructed with default initializer; users typically customize fields before use. Ownership: plain value type; no special destruction semantics beyond std::string. Dependent types StopBits, Parity, FlowControl, and TimeDuration are referenced from other headers and not defined here.

A POD-style configuration struct in the opendnp3 namespace that encapsulates TLS/SSL settings for a secure connection, including certificate/key file paths, allowed TLS protocol versions, and an OpenSSL cipher-list string. Used to pass TLS parameters to connection setup code. No destructor or special ownership semantics are defined; strings are owned by the struct.
direct_api_constructors: opendnp3::TLSConfig::TLSConfig(const std::string&, const std::string&, const std::string&, bool, bool, bool, bool, const std::string&)

objects.description: A stand-alone DNP3 decoder facade in the opendnp3 namespace. It exposes methods to decode link-layer (LPDU), transport-layer (TPDU), and application-layer (APDU) Protocol Data Units from a Buffer, delegating actual work to an internal DecoderImpl via a pimpl pointer. Constructed with a callback sink (IDecoderCallbacks) and a Logger. Exact semantics of decoding and lifetime management beyond RAII are not described in this header.
Forward-declared internal implementation class for Decoder (pimpl idiom). No definition is provided in this header; details are hidden in the implementation unit.

An interface-like base class in the opendnp3 namespace that disables copying (via Uncopyable) and provides protected virtual hooks to adjust an indentation level used during decoding/logging. The friend declaration grants the Indent class access to call these hooks. No public API is exposed here; derived classes are expected to implement behavior for PushIndent/PopIndent. Details about Indent and how these hooks are used are not present in this header.

A non-copyable base type referenced as a parent of IDecoderCallbacks. It is only included via header and not defined in this file; therefore its definition is unavailable here. Typically, such a class deletes copy constructor and copy assignment operator to prevent copying.

enum class AnalogOutputStatusQuality : uint8_t
{
  ONLINE = 0x1,
  RESTART = 0x2,
  COMM_LOST = 0x4,
  REMOTE_FORCED = 0x8,
  LOCAL_FORCED = 0x10,
  OVERRANGE = 0x20,
  REFERENCE_ERR = 0x40,
  RESERVED = 0x80
};
objects.description: Strongly-typed 8-bit enum defining the bitmask quality flags for Analog Output Status values in DNP3. Each enumerator represents a single bit; flags may be combined to describe data quality. Intended for use where quality tagging of analog output status points is required.

Helper spec struct providing conversion and formatting utilities for AnalogOutputStatusQuality. It offers functions to convert between the enum and its underlying uint8_t, obtain machine- and human-readable strings, and parse from string. Only declarations are present in this header; definitions are elsewhere.

objects.definition:
enum class AnalogQuality : uint8_t
{
  ONLINE = 0x1,
  RESTART = 0x2,
  COMM_LOST = 0x4,
  REMOTE_FORCED = 0x8,
  LOCAL_FORCED = 0x10,
  OVERRANGE = 0x20,
  REFERENCE_ERR = 0x40,
  RESERVED = 0x80
};
objects.description: Strongly-typed enum (scoped enum class) representing the bitmask quality flags for analog values in DNP3. Each bit indicates a specific quality condition such as ONLINE, RESTART, COMM_LOST, etc. Underlying type is uint8_t so it can be combined with bitwise operations after casting. Intended for tagging/inspecting quality on analog measurements.

Helper/specification struct that defines conversion and string utilities for AnalogQuality. Provides static helpers to convert to/from the underlying uint8_t, machine-readable and human-readable string forms, and parse from string. No data members; acts as a utility namespace for AnalogQuality.
Strongly-typed enum of DNP3 groups that can be used with the ASSIGN_CLASS function code. Values identify object types (e.g., binary inputs, counters) to which class assignments may be applied.

Traits/adapter struct for AssignClassType providing conversions between the enum and its underlying type, string names, and human-readable strings. Only static member declarations are provided here; definitions are elsewhere.
An enumeration type imported from opendnp3/gen/GroupVariation.h that identifies a DNP3 group/variation. It is only referenced here; no definition in this header.

objects.definition:
enum class BinaryOutputStatusQuality : uint8_t
{
  ONLINE = 0x1,
  RESTART = 0x2,
  COMM_LOST = 0x4,
  REMOTE_FORCED = 0x8,
  LOCAL_FORCED = 0x10,
  RESERVED1 = 0x20,
  RESERVED2 = 0x40,
  STATE = 0x80
};
objects.description: Scoped enum representing the quality bitmask for Binary Output Status values in DNP3. Each enumerator corresponds to a bit flag stored in an 8-bit field. Intended to encode communication and forcing state as well as the on/off state bit.

Helper/specification struct providing conversion utilities for BinaryOutputStatusQuality, including conversions to/from the underlying uint8_t type and to/from string representations. Only declarations are present here; definitions are provided elsewhere.

Built-in fixed-width unsigned 8-bit integer type referenced as the underlying type of BinaryOutputStatusQuality. Included here only if explicitly typedef’d in this header; since it is not, this entry should be ignored. Note: No custom typedef is defined in this header for uint8_t.

Standard library string type used as a parameter type in BinaryOutputStatusQualitySpec. Not defined in this header; per requirements, this referenced type should be ignored. Note: No custom typedef or class definition occurs here.
Strongly-typed enum (scoped enum) defining the bitmask flags that describe the quality of a binary point in DNP3. Underlying type is uint8_t. Flags can be OR'ed to represent combined quality states.

Helper/traits struct for BinaryQuality that provides conversion utilities between the enum and its underlying integer type, C-string names, and parsing from std::string. Only declarations are present here; definitions are elsewhere.

Strongly-typed enumeration of channel states in opendnp3. Values indicate lifecycle phases of a communication channel: CLOSED (idle/offline), OPENING (attempting to open), OPEN (active), and SHUTDOWN (permanently stopped). Backed by uint8_t.

Helper/specification struct providing conversions for opendnp3::ChannelState: to/from underlying uint8_t, to string and human-readable string, and from string. All members are static; the struct has no data and is not meant to be instantiated.

Strongly-typed enum describing the lifecycle/result states of an individual command point following Select-Before-Operate (SBO) or direct operate actions. Values range from initial/no response to select/operate success or various failure/mismatch cases.

Traits/utility struct for CommandPointState providing conversion helpers between the enum and its underlying type, C-strings, human-friendly strings, and parsing from std::string. Definitions are not provided here; only declarations exist in this header.

Helper spec struct that provides type conversion and string formatting/parsing utilities for TimeSyncMode. Offers conversions to/from the underlying uint8_t, machine-readable and human-readable strings, and parsing from std::string.
Strongly-typed 8-bit enumeration indicating which output (default, close, trip) to operate in a complementary two-output model per IEEE 1815-2012 Section A.8.1. RESERVED is kept for future use.

Specification/traits struct for TripCloseCode providing conversion utilities between the enum and its underlying type, string names, and human-readable strings. Definitions are not present in this header; only declarations are provided.

Value-type struct in namespace opendnp3 representing a link-layer address pair: 16-bit source and destination. Provides default and (source,destination) constructors, equality/inequality, Reverse() to swap endpoints, and a declaration of IsBroadcast() which indicates if the destination represents a broadcast address (definition not present in this header). Fields default to 0. No ownership semantics; trivially copyable.

Abstract callback interface for receiving optional link-layer events in the DNP3 stack. Methods provide notifications for link status changes, unknown addresses, and keep-alive activity. All methods have empty default implementations, so implementers may override as needed. Construction/destruction details are not provided in this header; typical usage is to subclass and provide overrides, then pass an instance to components that accept an ILinkListener.

Configuration struct for the DNP3 link layer within namespace opendnp3. Provides constructors to set master/outstation role, local/remote link-layer addresses, request timeout, and keep-alive interval. The default constructor is deleted; users must choose one of the provided constructors. The two-parameter (bool, bool) constructor is deprecated and retained for backward compatibility. GetAddresses() returns an Addresses value constructed from LocalAddr and RemoteAddr. TimeDuration semantics (e.g., Seconds/Minutes/Max) and Addresses are defined elsewhere.

Holds the parsed/constructed fields of an IEEE 1815 (DNP3) link-layer header within the opendnp3 stack. It records the link function code, whether the frame is from a master, the Frame Count Bit (FCB), the Flow Control/Direction From Control (FCV/DFC) flag, and the source/destination addresses. Two constructors are declared: a default and one that initializes all fields. Full semantics (e.g., valid flag combinations) are not documented here.
direct_api_constructors: opendnp3::LinkHeaderFields::LinkHeaderFields(LinkFunction func, bool isMaster, bool fcb, bool fcvdfc, Addresses addresses)

objects.description: Aggregates counters related to the DNP3 link layer and underlying channel. Provides two nested structs, Channel and Parser, that hold byte/frame counts and parsing error statistics. Default-constructible with all counters initialized to zero; also constructible from existing Channel and Parser snapshots. No dynamic resources; trivially copyable; safe to pass by value/reference.

Holds link-layer parser statistics: counts of received frames and various parse/validation errors (CRC errors, bad length, bad function code, FCV/FCB issues). All counters default to zero. Plain aggregate; no behavior defined here.

Holds channel I/O and state-change counters: open/close/open-fail events, bytes received/transmitted, and link frames transmitted. All counters default to zero. Plain aggregate; no behavior defined here.

Abstract callback interface for handling log messages emitted by the library. Users implement this to receive logs with module identifier, logger id string, log level, source location, and message. Lifetime and threading guarantees are not specified in this header. Implementations must provide the pure virtual log() method and may override the virtual destructor if needed.

Lightweight strongly-typed wrapper around a 32-bit module identifier value used for logging categorization. Holds an int32_t value and provides a default and explicit-from-int constructor. No behavior beyond storage.

Strongly-typed single-bit log level wrapper. Encapsulates a 32-bit integer bit flag with helpers: next() shifts to the next bit; equality operator compares underlying value. Used to define individual logging categories/flags.

Typed bitfield aggregating multiple LogLevel flags. Provides constructors from int32_t and LogLevel, bitwise OR and complement operations, membership test via is_set(), and factories for none() and everything(). Stores the underlying 32-bit mask.
Function declaration returning a C string name for a given LogLevel flag. No definition provided in this header.

Copyable facade class over a logging root that routes log messages to an ILogHandler with module, id, and level filtering. Holds shared ownership of immutable backend and settings. Provides detach methods to create derived loggers with different ids/levels, query/modify levels, and rename the logger id. Construction requires an ILogHandler backend and initial module/id/levels. Details of ModuleId, LogLevels, LogLevel, and ILogHandler are external to this header.
direct_api_constructors: opendnp3::Logger::Logger(const std::shared_ptr<ILogHandler>&, ModuleId, const std::string&, LogLevels)

objects.description: Configuration bundle for Logger instances: the module identifier, human-readable logger id string, and the enabled LogLevels mask. Stored and shared via std::shared_ptr by Logger to allow cheap copies and detached variants.

A small value-type class representing the result of issuing a command to a specific point in DNP3. It captures the originating header index, the point index, the final command state, and the command status (only meaningful when state is SUCCESS or SELECT_FAIL). It provides a value constructor and an equality check. No dynamic resources or ownership semantics are involved; it is a plain aggregate-like class with public data members.

objects.definition: class ICommandHeader;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an internal, non-public API class representing a command header element owned and managed by CommandSet. Only an incomplete type is exposed in this header to hide implementation details.

A value-type builder that aggregates one or more command headers for DNP3 operations. It owns a vector of shared pointers to internal ICommandHeader objects and provides constructors and helpers to add ControlRelayOutputBlock and AnalogOutput variants grouped by headers. Copy is disabled; moves are supported. Destruction is defined out-of-line to hide ICommandHeader implementation details.

Concrete final class implementing IListenCallbacks that provides default behavior for listen/accept events in the opendnp3 master stack. It exposes hooks to accept or reject connections and certificates, specify a first-frame timeout, react to the first link-layer frame, handle connection close, and report certificate errors. Actual behavior is defined in the corresponding implementation; this header only declares the interface. The helper SessionIdToString converts a session id to a string. Construction is via the default constructor; destruction is trivial.

Concrete final implementation of IMasterApplication that provides default no-op behavior for most callbacks, returns false for AssignClassDuringStartup, and leaves Now() to be defined elsewhere. Intended as a convenient default application object for DNP3 masters when custom behavior is not needed.

A small value-type class conveying metadata about a parsed DNP3 object header for ISOEHandler callbacks. It records the group/variation, qualifier, timestamp quality, whether the variation is an event, whether flags are present/valid, and the zero-based header index within the ASDU. Note: The constructor references IsEvent(gv_) and HasFlags(gv_), which are not defined in this header; they are presumed utility functions elsewhere in the library. No ownership semantics beyond plain fields; copyable/movable by default.
Forward-declared helper class used to serialize Header instances. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; its definition resides elsewhere.
Enumeration describing the wire-format style of a DNP3 object header (all objects, start/stop ranges using 8/16-bit indices, or limited counts using 8/16-bit).
Template representing an inclusive start/stop range for indices. This instantiation is for 8-bit indices.
Template representing an inclusive start/stop range for indices. This instantiation is for 16-bit indices.
Template representing a count of objects. This instantiation is for 8-bit counts.
Template representing a count of objects. This instantiation is for 16-bit counts.
Tagged-storage union holding the parameter payload for a Header depending on its HeaderType (8/16-bit range or count).

User-facing builder/value type used to specify a DNP3 object header to be serialized via HeaderWriter. It encapsulates the group/variation (via GroupVariationID), the header style (HeaderType), and the payload (HeaderUnion). Construct via the provided static factory methods; WriteTo emits the header to a HeaderWriter.

Pure-virtual interface in opendnp3 that dispatches DNP3 control commands from application code to a master. It defines two abstract operations for batched commands (SelectAndOperate and DirectOperate) and provides templated helpers to perform these operations on a single command at an index by internally creating a CommandSet. Concrete implementations are expected to manage request transmission and invoke the provided CommandResultCallbackT upon completion or failure. Ownership/lifetime is external; the interface itself does not manage resources. Details about CommandSet, CommandResultCallbackT, TaskConfig, and WithIndex are defined elsewhere.

Abstract class representing the result of a command task. It derives from ICollection<CommandPointResult> to expose iteration over individual CommandPointResult entries, and it carries a TaskCompletion summary field summarizing the overall task outcome. Construction requires a TaskCompletion value. The class is intended to be returned via callback after command operations. Ownership, lifecycle, and virtual interface come from the ICollection base (not defined here). Details like virtual destructor or additional methods are not shown in this header.

Abstract callback interface in opendnp3 invoked by the listener when new TCP/TLS connections arrive. Users implement this class to control acceptance of connections/certificates, provide a first-frame timeout, and receive events for first link-layer frame, connection close, and certificate verification errors. Pure virtual; no ownership semantics beyond typical interface usage are defined here.

Abstract interface class representing a running DNP3 master session. It inherits from IMasterOperations (for master-specific operations) and IStack (for common stack lifecycle/control). The class only declares a virtual defaulted destructor and defines no additional members in this header.

objects.definition: typedef std::function<void(const Header&)> WriteHeaderFunT;
objects.description: Alias for a callable taking a const Header& and returning void. Used by the master to allow user code to add headers to an assign-class request. Pointer type shown is to the alias itself, not to the callable object it might wrap.

Abstract interface for master application callbacks in an OpenDNP3 master. Inherits ILinkListener and IUTCTimeSource and provides virtual hooks for IIN reception, task lifecycle, and channel open/close. Also allows controlling and configuring an Assign Class task at startup. All methods have default no-op implementations; override as needed.

Abstract interface (pure virtual class) for master-side DNP3 operations. It extends ICommandProcessor and exposes methods to configure logging, create recurring scans, trigger one-shot scans, write TimeAndInterval objects, perform device restarts, and issue generic function-code operations. It has no data members or concrete behavior here; implementations are provided elsewhere.

Abstract interface in the opendnp3 namespace representing a permanently bound scan. It provides a virtual destructor and a single pure-virtual method Demand() that requests the scan be performed as soon as possible. Instances are expected to be provided by the library; this header defines the interface only.

Abstract interface in the opendnp3 namespace representing an ephemeral master session. It inherits from IMasterOperations (declared elsewhere). It provides a virtual destructor, a pure-virtual accessor for StackStatistics, and a pure-virtual method to initiate shutdown. Construction is via concrete implementations provided elsewhere; destruction should be through the virtual destructor. Details about StackStatistics and IMasterOperations are not defined in this header.

Abstract interface in the opendnp3 namespace for accepting/creating master sessions when a new connection is established. Users implement this class and return a shared_ptr<IMasterSession> from AcceptSession based on the provided session id, SOE handler, master application, and stack configuration. The class is purely virtual with a virtual destructor.

Abstract interface (pure virtual class) that applications implement to receive Sequence-Of-Events (SOE) callbacks from an opendnp3 master. It signals fragment boundaries and provides typed Process callbacks for each measurement/event type. Lifecycle: created by user code; no ownership semantics defined here; destructor is virtual and defaulted. No constructors are provided; implementers subclass and override all pure-virtual methods relevant to their use.

Abstract interface defining lifecycle callbacks for a task within the opendnp3 library. Users implement this to receive notifications when a task starts, completes with a TaskCompletion result, and is destroyed. No ownership semantics or memory management are specified here; it is a pure virtual interface with no data members.

Abstract interface in the opendnp3 namespace that provides a single pure-virtual method Now() to obtain the current UTC time as a UTCTimestamp. Intended to be implemented by platform-specific time sources. No destructor is declared, so deletion through this interface is only safe if the derived class ensures a virtual destructor elsewhere; usage likely expects references or ownership outside this interface.

Holds configuration parameters for an OpenDNP3 master instance. Fields control timeouts, time synchronization behavior, unsolicited messaging, integrity/event scan class masks, task retry/backoff and start timeouts, APDU fragment sizes, and index qualifier selection policy. No special construction beyond default initialization is required; values are value-initialized with sensible defaults. Destruction has no special requirements. Some member types (TimeDuration, ClassField, TimeSyncMode, IndexQualifierMode) are defined elsewhere.

Concrete final class implementing ISOEHandler that prints received DNP3 sequence-of-events (SOE) measurements and fragment boundaries to std::cout. Provides multiple Process overloads for common DNP3 measurement types and utilities to format values and timestamps. Creation is typically via the static Create() which returns a shared_ptr to the ISOEHandler interface.

A small value-type struct in the opendnp3 namespace that summarizes metadata about an APDU response: whether it was unsolicited and whether it is the first and/or final fragment of a multi-fragment response. It has a convenience constructor initializing the three boolean fields. No ownership semantics or special construction/destruction considerations beyond trivial POD-like use.

Concrete result type for a restart operation in opendnp3. Holds the overall task completion status and the time delay until restart. Default-constructs with summary set to TaskCompletion::FAILURE_NO_COMMS and an uninitialized/default TimeDuration. No ownership semantics are implied; it's a simple value-type with two public fields.

Type alias for a callback functor taking a const RestartOperationResult& and returning void. Used to receive the result of a restart operation asynchronously. This is an alias of std::function<void(const RestartOperationResult&)>.

Configuration object for master tasks in opendnp3. Encapsulates a TaskId and an optional ITaskCallback shared pointer. Provides convenience factory methods Default() and With(...) to create configurations with an undefined TaskId and either no callback or a specified callback. Default constructor is deleted; callers must use the parameterized ctor or the static helpers.

A small value-type class used to identify a task within the opendnp3 master stack. It wraps an integer id and a flag indicating whether the id is defined. Instances are constructed via the static factory methods Defined(id) and Undefined(). The default constructor is deleted, so callers must use the provided factories or the private constructor (not accessible externally). The class is trivially copyable and intended to be passed by value or stored; it does not own resources and requires no special destruction.

A small aggregate class conveying information about a DNP3 master task completion. It holds the task type, the completion status, and the task identifier. It is constructed directly via its value-initializing constructor. Note: MasterTaskType, TaskCompletion, and TaskId are referenced types from other headers and are not defined here.

Small immutable-ish value object exposing selected fields from a preverified X.509 certificate for application inspection and optional rejection. Holds chain depth, the SHA-1 certificate thumbprint, and the extracted subject name. Copying is disabled via private inheritance from Uncopyable. Default construction is disallowed; must be constructed with all fields provided.

Outstation-side container for application-controlled IIN (Internal Indications) flags in DNP3. It exposes boolean members representing specific IIN conditions (needTime, localControl, deviceTrouble, configCorrupt, eventBufferOverflow) and provides ToIIN() to convert the current flags to an IINField bitfield. Construction is default, members default to false. Destruction and copying use compiler defaults. Note: IINField is referenced from another header and not defined here.

Container struct that aggregates configuration maps for all DNP3 measurement and status types in an outstation database. Provides a default constructor and a constructor taking a uint16_t (presumably to apply a default configuration to all types). Each field maps 16-bit index to the corresponding MeasurementConfig-derived type. Exact semantics of the uint16_t constructor and individual config types are not defined in this header.

Concrete outstation application implementation providing default/example behavior. It implements IOutstationApplication and IDnpTimeSource methods with basic policies: supports absolute time writes, does not support time-and-interval, supports assign class recording (no-op in this header), and reports unsupported restarts. It maintains a refresh period and last written time to determine time validity/needs. Constructor accepts a TimeDuration for time sync refresh rate.

Configuration struct within namespace opendnp3 that specifies per-type maximum event buffer sizes for an outstation. Uses a preallocated heap buffer sized to the sum of all maxima (TotalEvents). Provides a convenience factory (AllTypes) to set the same maximum for all event types and a constructor to set per-type limits. Fields are public and directly settable. Proper usage involves choosing counts appropriate for polling frequency and memory constraints. Destruction/ownership is trivial (POD-like); no special lifetime rules indicated. The actual definitions of AllTypes and TotalEvents are not present in this header.

objects.definition:
namespace opendnp3
{

/**
 * Interface used to dispatch SELECT / OPERATE / DIRECT OPERATE (Binary/Analog output) from the outstation to
 * application code.
 *
 * The ITransactable sub-interface is used to determine the start and end of an ASDU containing commands.
 */
class ICommandHandler
{
public:
    virtual ~ICommandHandler() = default;

    /**
     * called when a command APDU begins processing
     */
    virtual void Begin() = 0;

    /**
     * called when a command APDU ends processing
     */
    virtual void End() = 0;

    /**
     * Ask if the application supports a ControlRelayOutputBlock - group 12 variation 1
     *
     * @param command command to operate
     * @param index index of the command
     * @return result of request
     */
    virtual CommandStatus Select(const ControlRelayOutputBlock& command, uint16_t index) = 0;

    /**
     * Operate a ControlRelayOutputBlock - group 12 variation 1
     *
     * @param command command to operate
     * @param index index of the command
     * @param handler interface for loading measurement changes
     * @param opType the operation type the outstation received.
     * @return result of request
     */
    virtual CommandStatus Operate(const ControlRelayOutputBlock& command,
                                  uint16_t index,
                                  IUpdateHandler& handler,
                                  OperateType opType)
        = 0;

    /**
     * Ask if the application supports a 16 bit analog output - group 41 variation 2
     *
     * @param command command to operate
     * @param index index of the command
     * @return result of request
     */
    virtual CommandStatus Select(const AnalogOutputInt16& command, uint16_t index) = 0;

    /**
     * Ask if the application supports a 16 bit analog output - group 41 variation 2
     *
     * @param command command to operate
     * @param index index of the command
     * @param handler interface for loading measurement changes
     * @param opType the operation type the outstation received.
     * @return result of request
     */
    virtual CommandStatus Operate(const AnalogOutputInt16& command,
                                  uint16_t index,
                                  IUpdateHandler& handler,
                                  OperateType opType)
        = 0;

    /**
     * Ask if the application supports a 32 bit analog output - group 41 variation 1
     *
     * @param command command to operate
     * @param index index of the command
     * @return result of request
     */
    virtual CommandStatus Select(const AnalogOutputInt32& command, uint16_t index) = 0;

    /**
     * Operate a 32 bit analog output - group 41 variation 1
     *
     * @param command command to operate
     * @param index index of the command
     * @param handler interface for loading measurement changes
     * @param opType the operation type the outstation received.
     * @return result of request
     */
    virtual CommandStatus Operate(const AnalogOutputInt32& command,
                                  uint16_t index,
                                  IUpdateHandler& handler,
                                  OperateType opType)
        = 0;

    /**
     * Ask if the application supports a single precision, floating point analog output - group 41 variation 3
     *
     * @param command command to operate
     * @param index index of the command
     * @return result of request
     */
    virtual CommandStatus Select(const AnalogOutputFloat32& command, uint16_t index) = 0;

    /**
     * Operate a single precision, floating point analog output - group 41 variation 3
     *
     * @param command command to operate
     * @param index index of the command
     * @param handler interface for loading measurement changes
     * @param opType the operation type the outstation received.
     * @return result of request
     */
    virtual CommandStatus Operate(const AnalogOutputFloat32& command,
                                  uint16_t index,
                                  IUpdateHandler& handler,
                                  OperateType opType)
        = 0;

    /**
     * Ask if the application supports a double precision, floating point analog output - group 41 variation 4
     *
     * @param command command to operate
     * @param index index of the command
     * @return result of request
     */
    virtual CommandStatus Select(const AnalogOutputDouble64& command, uint16_t index) = 0;

    /**
     * Operate a double precision, floating point analog output - group 41 variation 4
     *
     * @param command command to operate
     * @param index index of the command
     * @param handler interface for loading measurement changes
     * @param opType the operation type the outstation received.
     * @return result of request
     */
    virtual CommandStatus Operate(const AnalogOutputDouble64& command,
                                  uint16_t index,
                                  IUpdateHandler& handler,
                                  OperateType opType)
        = 0;
};

} // namespace opendnp3
objects.description: Abstract interface in opendnp3 for handling DNP3 command processing (SELECT/OPERATE/DIRECT OPERATE). Users implement this to accept, validate, and execute ControlRelayOutputBlock and various AnalogOutput commands, with Begin/End bracketing an APDU of commands. No data members; lifetime managed by caller. All methods are pure virtual, so there is no construction beyond default; destruction is via virtual destructor.

Abstract time source interface within the opendnp3 namespace that provides the current DNPTime used for operations such as freezing counters. Although named like an interface, it provides a virtual (not pure) method with a default implementation returning an invalid timestamp; users typically subclass and override Now() to provide a meaningful time.

Abstract interface (class) for a running DNP3 outstation. It inherits from IStack (declared elsewhere) and defines control methods for logging filters, setting the Restart IIN bit, and applying measurement Updates. Being a pure-virtual interface, it has no data members and is intended to be implemented by a concrete outstation. Destruction is virtual and defaulted.

Abstract interface in namespace opendnp3 providing application-level callbacks for an outstation (server) excluding control requests. It derives from ILinkListener and IDnpTimeSource (both defined elsewhere). Methods allow enabling and handling of absolute time writes, TimeAndInterval writes, class assignment persistence, application-controlled IIN bits, restart capability and execution, and a notification when a CONFIRM is processed. Default implementations indicate unsupported features and no-ops; users should subclass and override as needed.

Abstract interface in namespace opendnp3 for updating various DNP3 measurement types in a database or handler. It defines pure-virtual methods to update specific measurement types, freeze counters, update octet strings and time/interval values, and modify flags ranges. Implementations should perform existence checks and event generation according to EventMode. Ownership and lifetime are external; this interface has a virtual destructor and no state.
Concrete config for binary points. Inherits event and static variation settings from EventConfig<BinaryInfo>; contains no additional fields.
Concrete config for double-bit binary points. Inherits event and static variation settings from EventConfig<DoubleBitBinaryInfo>.
Concrete config for analog points. Inherits static/event variation and adds deadband via DeadbandConfig<AnalogInfo>.
Concrete config for counter points. Extends with deadband through DeadbandConfig<CounterInfo>.
Concrete config for frozen counter points. Provides deadband and variation settings via DeadbandConfig<FrozenCounterInfo>.
Concrete config for Binary Output Status points. Inherits event/static variation settings from EventConfig<BinaryOutputStatusInfo>.
Concrete config for Analog Output Status points. Includes deadband and variation settings via DeadbandConfig<AnalogOutputStatusInfo>.
Concrete config for octet string points. Inherits event/static variation settings via EventConfig<OctetStringInfo>.
Concrete config for Time and Interval points. Provides static variation settings via StaticConfig<TimeAndIntervalInfo>.
Empty config placeholder for Security Statistic points. No fields or defaults are defined in this header; purpose is inferred as a type token for future configuration options.

A small final class that models the number of allowed retries for unsolicited responses in the opendnp3 stack. It supports two construction modes: a fixed, bounded retry count and an infinite retry mode. The class tracks the current retry attempt (numRetries), the configured maximum (maxNumRetries), and whether it is operating in infinite mode. Retry() presumably advances/indicates whether another retry should be attempted, and Reset() resets the internal counter. Exact semantics (e.g., whether Retry() increments or just tests) are not documented in this header and must be inferred from implementation elsewhere.

OutstationConfig groups configuration for an opendnp3 outstation. It holds OutstationParams governing general behavior (e.g., unsolicited responses, time sync, class/variation defaults) and an EventBufferConfig specifying event buffer sizes. Detailed semantics depend on the definitions of OutstationParams and EventBufferConfig, which are declared elsewhere.

Configuration struct defining static parameters for an outstation session in the DNP3 stack. It includes APDU control limits, timeouts for select/operate and confirmations, unsolicited retry policy, maximum fragment sizes, unsolicited behavior, allowed static type bitfield for class 0 responses, class mask for unsolicited events, and an option to accept requests from any master. Many member types (TimeDuration, NumRetries, StaticTypeBitField, ClassField) are defined in other headers and are referenced here. Construction is via aggregate initialization; no special constructor/destructor is defined. Defaults are provided inline.

Composite configuration struct for assembling a full DNP3 outstation stack configuration. It embeds DatabaseConfig, OutstationConfig, and LinkConfig. The default constructor initializes link with a parameter of false (per LinkConfig(bool) semantics defined elsewhere). The second constructor allows providing an initial DatabaseConfig while still initializing link(false). Ownership-wise, this type contains and manages the three configuration objects by value.

Concrete mock ICommandHandler implementation for examples/demos. It counts Begin/End/Select/Operate calls and replies to all command selections/operations with a fixed CommandStatus. Provides overridable DoSelect/DoOperate hooks per command type. Requires types like ICommandHandler, IUpdateHandler, CommandStatus, OperateType, and command value types to be available from included headers.
Specialization of SimpleCommandHandler that always uses CommandStatus::SUCCESS. Provides a static Create() helper returning a shared_ptr<ICommandHandler>.

Opaque value-type bitfield in namespace opendnp3 that represents a subset of static measurement types using a 16-bit mask. Provides default constructor (empty set), a mask-based constructor, AllTypes() factory returning all bits set, IsSet(...) to test membership against a StaticTypeBitmask flag, and Except(...) to produce a new bitfield with a given flag cleared. Internals: stores a private uint16_t mask. Destruction/ownership: trivial POD-like struct; no special lifetime rules. Note: depends on enum-like StaticTypeBitmask (declared elsewhere) for flag values.

Concrete, final implementation of opendnp3::IUpdateHandler that accumulates measurement updates and modifications, then produces an Updates object via Build(). Methods enqueue updates for various DNP3 measurement types; internal storage is a shared pointer to shared_updates_t (defined elsewhere). Construction and destruction details are not provided here; class is declared but not defined inline beyond its interface in this header.

objects.definition: typedef std::function<void(IUpdateHandler&)> update_func_t;
objects.description: Alias for a callable that takes an IUpdateHandler reference and returns void. Used to represent a single update operation to be applied to an IUpdateHandler.

objects.definition: typedef std::vector<update_func_t> shared_updates_t;
objects.description: Alias for a sequence (std::vector) of update_func_t callables. Represents a collection of update operations that can be applied in order.

Lightweight handle over a shared collection of update_func_t objects. Provides Apply to execute all stored updates on an IUpdateHandler and IsEmpty to query emptiness. Constructible only within the component (private ctor) and by the friend UpdateBuilder (defined elsewhere). Holds a shared_ptr to the underlying vector and may be empty (nullptr).

A simple immutable view of a byte buffer within the opendnp3 namespace. It stores a pointer to constant byte data and its length. The struct does not own the memory it points to and provides no deallocation; users must ensure the pointed-to memory remains valid for the lifetime of the view.

A utility class used to prevent instantiation, copying, and assignment. By deleting the default constructor, copy constructor, and copy-assignment operator in the private section, it enforces a static-only usage pattern for classes that inherit from it or to serve as a pattern reference. It has no data members or functions and cannot be constructed directly.

Strongly-typed wrapper around std::chrono::steady_clock::duration for representing millisecond-based time durations in the opendnp3 API. Provides factory methods for constructing durations from milliseconds, seconds, and minutes, query/utility methods (e.g., IsNegative, ToString, Double), comparison operators, and exposes the underlying chrono duration as a public member named value. Construction details for Min/Max/Zero and conversion ranges are not visible here. Note: class declares friend class Timestamp but that type is only forward-declared here and not defined in this header.

A strongly-typed wrapper around std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point representing a monotonic timestamp in the opendnp3 namespace. Supports min/max sentinels, arithmetic with TimeDuration, and comparison operations. The value field stores the underlying time_point. Details like the exact semantics of Min/Max and overflow handling are implied: addition/subtraction with TimeDuration caps at maximum value; other behaviors are per implementation in the source file, which is not shown here.

Base class intended to be inherited to disable copy construction and copy assignment while still allowing default construction, destruction, and move operations. Classes deriving from Uncopyable become move-enabled but non-copyable, enforcing unique ownership or preventing unintended copies.

A simple strong-typed wrapper around a 64-bit millisecond count since the Unix epoch (UTC). Provides a default constructor initializing to 0 and a value constructor taking milliseconds since epoch. Public member msSinceEpoch holds the timestamp value. No additional behavior, ownership, or destruction requirements are indicated.

functions.name: opendnp3::ConsoleLogger::log
functions.signature: void opendnp3::ConsoleLogger::log(opendnp3::ModuleId module, const char* id, opendnp3::LogLevel level, const char* location, const char* message)
functions.description: Implements ILogHandler::log to print a formatted log message to the console. Typical usage is via the logging subsystem which invokes this callback for each log event; callers normally do not invoke it directly. Thread-safety is internally managed via a mutex; behavior includes optional inclusion of source location based on the instance configuration.
requirements: module must be a valid opendnp3::ModuleId value.
level must be a valid opendnp3::LogLevel value.
id must point to a valid, null-terminated C-string (may be empty if allowed by the wider logging API; nullability is unknown).
location must point to a valid, null-terminated C-string (may be ignored if the instance is configured not to print location; nullability is unknown).
message must point to a valid, null-terminated C-string describing the log entry (nullability is unknown).
May be called concurrently from multiple threads; the method guards internal state with a mutex.

count is an 8-bit value (0–255) by type; values beyond this range cannot be represented.

The value argument must be a valid instance of Spec::meas_t.

functions.name: opendnp3::SimpleEventCell<Spec>::IsEvent
functions.signature:
template <class Spec>
bool opendnp3::SimpleEventCell<Spec>::IsEvent(const typename Spec::config_t& config, const typename Spec::meas_t& newValue) const
functions.description: Determines if newValue constitutes an event relative to the stored lastEvent for simple (no-deadband) measurements. Delegates the decision to Spec::IsEvent(lastEvent, newValue). The config parameter is accepted to conform to a common interface but is not used here.
requirements: Template parameter Spec must define type aliases meas_t and config_t.
Spec must provide a static function or callable IsEvent(const Spec::meas_t& last, const Spec::meas_t& next) returning bool.
The newValue argument must be a valid instance of Spec::meas_t.
The config argument must be a valid instance of Spec::config_t (even though unused in this implementation).
The object’s lastEvent value is used as the comparison baseline; it is default-constructed by EventCellBase and should be updated via SetEventValue as appropriate before calling.

functions.name: opendnp3::DeadbandEventCell<Spec>::IsEvent
functions.signature:
template <class Spec>
bool opendnp3::DeadbandEventCell<Spec>::IsEvent(const typename Spec::config_t& config, const typename Spec::meas_t& newValue) const
functions.description: Determines if newValue is an event relative to lastEvent for measurements that support deadbanding. Delegates to Spec::IsEvent(lastEvent, newValue, config.deadband), allowing the Spec to apply a deadband threshold contained in the provided config.
requirements: Template parameter Spec must define type aliases meas_t and config_t.
config_t must provide a member named deadband accessible by this function and of a type acceptable to Spec::IsEvent.
Spec must provide a static function or callable IsEvent(const Spec::meas_t& last, const Spec::meas_t& next, decltype(config.deadband) deadband) returning bool.
The newValue argument must be a valid instance of Spec::meas_t.
The config argument must be a valid instance of Spec::config_t with its deadband member properly initialized.
The object’s lastEvent value is used as the comparison baseline; it is default-constructed by EventCellBase and should be updated via SetEventValue as appropriate before calling.

functions.name: opendnp3::measurements::IsEvent
functions.signature:
template <class T, class U>
bool opendnp3::measurements::IsEvent(const T& val1, const T& val2, T deadband)
functions.description: Determines whether a change between two values constitutes an event by comparing the absolute difference |val2 - val1| against a deadband threshold. The implementation computes the difference in an auxiliary type U (to avoid issues with unsigned T and std::abs) and returns true if the difference is strictly greater than deadband. Use this template when comparing plain numeric-like values where you can select an appropriate intermediate type U to hold the difference without ambiguity or overflow risk.
requirements: T must support comparison operator > (used as val2 > val1).
T must be convertible to U via static_cast<U>(T).
U must support subtraction (operator-) between two U values and yield a type comparable with T.
The expression (static_cast<U>(val2) - static_cast<U>(val1)) must be well-formed and not overflow U in the expected operating range.
The result type U must be comparable to T using operator> (as in diff > deadband) after usual arithmetic conversions.
val1 and val2 must be valid references to initialized objects of type T.
deadband is interpreted as a threshold; it is compared using a strict greater-than relationship (diff > deadband).
