functions.description: Returns a constant C-string with a human-friendly description of the given TripCloseCode. Intended for user-facing messages.
requirements: arg must be a valid opendnp3::TripCloseCode value.
The returned pointer refers to an internal static string; the caller must not modify or free it.
Exact wording is not specified in the header and may differ from the enum identifier.

functions.name: opendnp3::TripCloseCodeSpec::from_string
functions.description: Parses a string and returns the corresponding TripCloseCode enum value. Typically accepts symbolic names matching the enum constants; exact parsing rules (case-sensitivity, whitespace) are not specified in the header.
requirements: arg should match one of the recognized symbolic names for TripCloseCode (e.g., "NUL", "CLOSE", "TRIP", "RESERVED").
Behavior for unrecognized strings is unspecified; callers should only supply valid names.
The input string must be a valid std::string reference; no null termination assumptions beyond std::string semantics.

functions.name: opendnp3::Addresses::Addresses
functions.description: Default constructor for opendnp3::Addresses. Initializes source and destination to 0. Useful when you want to declare an address pair and assign fields later.
requirements: None beyond default-constructibility; resulting source and destination are initialized to 0.

functions.name: opendnp3::Addresses::Reverse
functions.description: Returns a new Addresses instance with source and destination swapped. Typically used to generate the reciprocal address pair for a response or opposite-direction frame.
requirements: The invoking Addresses instance must be initialized (either default-constructed and subsequently assigned, or value-constructed).

functions.name: opendnp3::Addresses::operator==
functions.description: Equality operator comparing both source and destination fields for exact equality.
requirements: Both this and other must refer to valid, initialized Addresses instances.

functions.name: opendnp3::Addresses::operator!=
functions.description: Inequality operator; logical negation of operator== comparing source and destination.
requirements: Both this and other must refer to valid, initialized Addresses instances.

functions.name: opendnp3::Addresses::IsBroadcast
functions.description: Returns true if the address pair represents a broadcast condition. Exact criteria are not defined in this header; likely based on a reserved destination value in the DNP3 specification. Use to detect frames intended for all stations.
requirements: The invoking Addresses instance must be initialized.

functions.name: opendnp3::ILinkListener::OnStateChange
functions.description: Callback invoked when the link-layer reset/unreset state changes. Override in a derived class to observe link status transitions; the base implementation is a no-op. Typically used by applications integrating with the DNP3 stack to monitor link state.
requirements: value must be a valid opendnp3::LinkStatus enumeration value.
No additional requirements are documented; base implementation performs no work.

functions.name: opendnp3::ILinkListener::OnUnknownDestinationAddress
functions.description: Callback invoked when a link-layer frame is received that targets an unknown destination address. Override to log, count, or react to frames not addressed to any configured endpoint. Base implementation is a no-op.
requirements: destination is a 16-bit link-layer address; no specific range constraints beyond uint16_t are documented.
No additional requirements are documented; base implementation performs no work.

functions.name: opendnp3::ILinkListener::OnUnknownSourceAddress
functions.description: Callback invoked when a link-layer frame is received from an unknown source address. Override to log or handle unexpected sources. Base implementation is a no-op.
requirements: source is a 16-bit link-layer address; no specific range constraints beyond uint16_t are documented.
No additional requirements are documented; base implementation performs no work.

functions.name: opendnp3::ILinkListener::OnKeepAliveInitiated
functions.description: Notification that the keep-alive timer elapsed and a keep-alive (request link status) was initiated. This is not a failure indication. Override to observe periodic keep-alive starts. Base implementation is a no-op.
requirements: No parameters. No explicit requirements documented; base implementation performs no work.

functions.name: opendnp3::ILinkListener::OnKeepAliveFailure
functions.description: Notification that a keep-alive (request link status) did not receive a response. Override to detect keep-alive failures (e.g., for logging or retry strategies). Base implementation is a no-op.
requirements: No parameters. No explicit requirements documented; base implementation performs no work.

functions.name: opendnp3::ILinkListener::OnKeepAliveSuccess
functions.description: Notification that a keep-alive (request link status) received a valid response. Override to track successful keep-alive exchanges. Base implementation is a no-op.
requirements: No parameters. No explicit requirements documented; base implementation performs no work.

functions.name: opendnp3::LinkConfig::LinkConfig
functions.description: Deleted default constructor for LinkConfig. Prevents creating an uninitialized link-layer configuration; callers must use one of the provided explicit constructors.
requirements: This constructor cannot be called; attempting to use it will result in a compile-time error.
Use one of the available explicit constructors to create a valid LinkConfig instance.

functions.name: opendnp3::LinkConfig::GetAddresses
functions.description: Returns an Addresses object built from the current LocalAddr and RemoteAddr fields. Useful for passing link-layer addressing as a single object.
requirements: The LinkConfig instance must have been constructed via a valid constructor before calling this method.
No side effects; callable on const instances.

functions.name: opendnp3::LinkHeaderFields::LinkHeaderFields
functions.description: Default constructor for a container of DNP3 link-layer header fields. It creates a LinkHeaderFields instance without setting any explicit values in this header file. Intended for constructing an object and assigning its members later. Exact default values (if any) are unknown from this header and may be defined in the implementation.
requirements: After construction, do not assume func, isFromMaster, fcb, fcvdfc, or addresses have meaningful values unless you set them explicitly (the header does not specify default member values).
Initialize or assign all fields to valid values before using the object in link-layer operations.

functions.name: opendnp3::LinkHeaderFields::LinkHeaderFields
functions.signature: opendnp3::LinkHeaderFields::LinkHeaderFields(opendnp3::LinkFunction func, bool isMaster, bool fcb, bool fcvdfc, opendnp3::Addresses addresses)
functions.description: Value-initializing constructor for a DNP3 link-layer header description. It sets the link function code, whether the frame is from a master, the frame count bit (FCB), the FCV/DFC bit, and the link-layer source/destination addresses. Use this to fully specify link header fields when forming or interpreting a link-layer frame.
requirements: func must be a valid opendnp3::LinkFunction enumeration value.
isMaster indicates the frame origin role; pass true for master-originated frames and false for outstation-originated frames.
fcb should reflect the intended frame count bit state for the session/sequence; toggle rules are protocol-specific and not specified in this header.
fcvdfc represents the FCV/DFC bit; its precise semantics depend on master vs. outstation role and are not specified in this header.
addresses must contain valid link-layer addressing appropriate for the application (source/destination as required by opendnp3::Addresses).

functions.name: opendnp3::ILogHandler::~ILogHandler
functions.description: Virtual destructor of the ILogHandler interface. Ensures derived classes can be destroyed safely via a base-class pointer, releasing any resources held by the implementation. Normally invoked implicitly when an ILogHandler implementation instance goes out of scope or is deleted.
requirements: The object must have been properly constructed before destruction.
Do not use the object after its destructor has run (no use-after-free).
If deleting via a base pointer, the dynamic type must be a valid ILogHandler implementation allocated with a compatible allocator.
Any resources owned by derived implementations should be released during destruction.

functions.name: opendnp3::ILogHandler::log
functions.signature: virtual void log(ModuleId module, const char* id, LogLevel level, const char* location, const char* message) = 0;
functions.description: Pure virtual callback invoked for each log message emitted by the stack. Implementations should process or forward the log entry identified by the logger id, module, log level bitfield, source location, and message text. Typical usage is to subclass ILogHandler and implement this method to integrate with an application or external logging system.
requirements: This method must be implemented by any concrete ILogHandler subclass (pure virtual).
module must be a valid ModuleId value as defined in opendnp3/logging/LogLevels.h.
level is a bitfield LogLevel value as defined in opendnp3/logging/LogLevels.h and should be interpreted as such by the implementation.
id must point to a valid, null-terminated C string for the duration of the call; ownership is not transferred.
location must point to a valid, null-terminated C string for the duration of the call; ownership is not transferred.
message must point to a valid, null-terminated C string for the duration of the call; ownership is not transferred.
Implementations must not modify the input strings (all are const).
If the implementation retains any of the provided strings after return, it must copy them, as the original memory may not remain valid.

functions.name: opendnp3::ModuleId::ModuleId
functions.description: Default constructor for ModuleId. Initializes value to 0. Used to create an empty/unspecified module identifier.

functions.name: opendnp3::LogLevel::LogLevel
functions.description: Default constructor for LogLevel. Initializes value to 0 (no flag set).

functions.name: opendnp3::LogLevel::next
functions.description: Returns a new LogLevel whose bit value is the current value shifted left by one. Intended to enumerate the next log level/flag.
requirements: > The operation is a left shift on a signed 32-bit integer; very large input values may overflow or produce undefined behavior in C++ if shifting into/sign beyond range. Callers should avoid inputs that would overflow when shifted left by 1.

functions.name: opendnp3::LogLevel::operator==
functions.description: Equality comparison for LogLevel based on the underlying integer value.
requirements: > other must be a valid LogLevel reference.

functions.name: opendnp3::LogLevels::LogLevels
functions.description: Default constructor for LogLevels. Initializes the bitfield to 0 (no levels enabled).

functions.name: opendnp3::LogLevels::none
functions.description: Factory returning a LogLevels instance with no bits set (no logging enabled).

functions.name: opendnp3::LogLevels::everything
functions.description: Factory returning a LogLevels instance with all bits set (all logging enabled). Uses bitwise complement of 0 on a 32-bit signed integer.

functions.name: opendnp3::LogLevels::is_set
functions.description: Checks whether the specified LogLevel bit is set in this LogLevels bitmask.
requirements: > level should correspond to the bit to test; typically a single-bit LogLevel.

functions.name: opendnp3::LogLevels::operator~
functions.description: Returns a new LogLevels with all bits inverted relative to this instance.

functions.name: opendnp3::LogLevels::operator|=
functions.description: Bitwise-OR assignment with a single LogLevel, enabling that level in this bitmask.
requirements: > other should typically represent a single-bit LogLevel flag.

functions.name: opendnp3::LogLevels::operator|
functions.description: Bitwise-OR with a single LogLevel, producing a new LogLevels with that level enabled in addition to the current bits.
requirements: > other should typically represent a single-bit LogLevel flag.

functions.name: opendnp3::LogLevels::get_value
functions.description: Returns the underlying 32-bit integer bitmask value for this LogLevels instance.

functions.name: opendnp3::LogFlagToString
functions.description: Converts a LogLevel flag to a human-readable C-string. Intended to map known log level flags to their names (e.g., EVENT, ERR, etc.). Implementation details are not provided in this header.
requirements: > flag should represent a known LogLevel value to obtain a meaningful name.
- The lifetime/ownership of the returned const char* is unknown from this header; assume it points to static or internal storage unless otherwise documented.

functions.name: opendnp3::Logger::Logger
functions.signature: opendnp3::Logger::Logger(const std::shared_ptr<opendnp3::ILogHandler>& backend, opendnp3::ModuleId moduleid, const std::string& id, opendnp3::LogLevels levels)
functions.description: Constructs a Logger bound to a logging backend, a module identifier, a logger id string, and a set of enabled log levels. Use this to create a copyable logger facade that can emit messages via the provided ILogHandler. If backend is null, the logger is effectively a no-op.
requirements: backend may be null; when null, calls to log() will be ignored
moduleid may be any valid opendnp3::ModuleId value (no additional constraints stated)
id should be a valid std::string identifying the logger (no specific format required)
levels should be a valid LogLevels bitmask/set selecting enabled levels (no additional constraints stated)

functions.name: opendnp3::Logger::empty
functions.description: Factory that returns a no-op Logger with a null backend, module id 0, empty id string, and no enabled levels. Useful as a placeholder when logging is disabled or not yet configured.
requirements: None; returned logger is valid but will not emit logs

functions.name: opendnp3::Logger::log
functions.signature: void opendnp3::Logger::log(const opendnp3::LogLevel& level, const char* location, const char* message)
functions.description: Emits a log entry through the backend handler using the logger's current module, id, and enabled levels. If the backend is null, the call is a no-op. Typical usage is to pass the log level, the call site (e.g., function or file/line), and a message string.
requirements: backend must be non-null for output to occur; if null the call does nothing
location must point to a valid null-terminated C string
message must point to a valid null-terminated C string
level should be a valid LogLevel value recognized by the backend
Message length limits are not enforced here; any truncation or size constraints (e.g., max_log_entry_size) would be handled downstream if applicable

functions.name: opendnp3::Logger::detach
functions.description: Creates a new Logger that shares the same backend and log levels but uses a different id string. Use this to derive component-specific child loggers from a parent.
requirements: id should be a valid std::string; no specific format required
Resulting Logger shares Settings with siblings created via this path; changes to levels or id on one may affect others if they share the same Settings instance

functions.name: opendnp3::Logger::detach
functions.signature: opendnp3::Logger opendnp3::Logger::detach(const std::string& id, opendnp3::LogLevels levels) const
functions.description: Creates a new Logger with the same backend and module but a different id and a specific set of enabled log levels. Use to derive a child logger with an overridden id and level mask.
requirements: id should be a valid std::string; no specific format required
levels should be a valid LogLevels set
The returned Logger has its own Settings instance (id and levels) but shares the same backend

functions.name: opendnp3::Logger::detach
functions.description: Creates a new Logger with the same backend, module, and id but with a different set of enabled log levels. Use to derive a logger variant that filters on a different level mask.
requirements: levels should be a valid LogLevels set
The returned Logger has its own Settings instance (id and levels) but shares the same backend

functions.name: opendnp3::Logger::is_enabled
functions.description: Checks if the specified log level is currently enabled for this Logger. Returns false if there is no backend or the level is not set in the current LogLevels.
requirements: level should be a valid LogLevel value
No side effects; safe to call at any time

functions.name: opendnp3::Logger::get_levels
functions.description: Returns the current set of enabled log levels associated with this Logger's Settings. Useful to inspect or snapshot the current filter mask.
requirements: None

functions.name: opendnp3::Logger::set_levels
functions.description: Replaces the current set of enabled log levels in the shared Settings with the given filter mask. This affects all Logger instances that share the same Settings.
requirements: filters should be a valid LogLevels set
Thread-safety is not specified; callers should ensure any required external synchronization if used across threads

functions.name: opendnp3::Logger::rename
functions.description: Changes the logger id string in the shared Settings. Affects this Logger and any other instances sharing the same Settings.
requirements: id should be a valid std::string; no specific format required
Thread-safety is not specified; callers should ensure any required external synchronization if used across threads

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandPointResult::CommandPointResult
functions.signature: opendnp3::CommandPointResult::CommandPointResult(uint32_t headerIndex_, uint16_t index_, opendnp3::CommandPointState state_, opendnp3::CommandStatus status_)
functions.description: Constructs a CommandPointResult with explicit values for the header index, point index, final command state, and command status. Use this to report the outcome of a command operation for a single point.
requirements: headerIndex_ is the 0-based index of the header when the request was made.
index_ is the index of the command that was requested.
status_ is only meaningful if state_ == opendnp3::CommandPointState::SUCCESS or state_ == opendnp3::CommandPointState::SELECT_FAIL; callers should not rely on status_ otherwise.
All arguments must be provided; there is no default constructor in this header.

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandPointResult::Equals
functions.description: Compares this CommandPointResult to another for equality. Returns true if and only if headerIndex, index, state, and status are all equal.
requirements: other must reference a valid CommandPointResult object.
No side effects; safe to call on const instances.

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandSet::~CommandSet
functions.description: Destructor for CommandSet. Releases any internal resources and owned ICommandHeader objects. Usage: automatically invoked when a CommandSet instance goes out of scope or is destroyed.
requirements: Do not use references returned by StartHeader<T>() after the CommandSet is destroyed (lifetime requirement).

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandSet::CommandSet
functions.description: Default constructor. Constructs an empty CommandSet with no headers. Usage: create, then populate via Add<T>(...) or StartHeader<T>().

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandSet::CommandSet
functions.description: Move constructor. Transfers ownership of any headers from another CommandSet, leaving the source in a valid but unspecified (typically empty) state. Usage: enables efficient transfer, e.g., returning a CommandSet from a function.
requirements: After the move, do not use any previously obtained references (e.g., from StartHeader<T>()) from the moved-from object.

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandSet::CommandSet
functions.description: Constructs a CommandSet initialized with a header of ControlRelayOutputBlock commands created from the provided Indexed items. Usage: aggregate one or more CROB commands with indices in a single expression.
requirements: Each element must be an Indexed<ControlRelayOutputBlock> with a valid index for the intended target (specific validity not enforced here).
The initializer list may be empty; if empty, the resulting CommandSet contains no headers.

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandSet::CommandSet
functions.description: Constructs a CommandSet initialized with a header of AnalogOutputInt16 commands created from the provided Indexed items.
requirements: Each element must be an Indexed<AnalogOutputInt16>.
The initializer list may be empty; if empty, the resulting CommandSet contains no headers.

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandSet::CommandSet
functions.description: Constructs a CommandSet initialized with a header of AnalogOutputInt32 commands created from the provided Indexed items.
requirements: Each element must be an Indexed<AnalogOutputInt32>.
The initializer list may be empty; if empty, the resulting CommandSet contains no headers.

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandSet::Add
functions.description: Convenience method to append a complete header of commands of type T to the CommandSet from an initializer_list. If the list is empty, the call is a no-op. Internally, starts a header for T and adds each (value,index) pair.
requirements: T must be one of: ControlRelayOutputBlock, AnalogOutputInt16, AnalogOutputInt32, AnalogOutputFloat32, or AnalogOutputDouble64 (only these specializations of StartHeader<T>() exist).
The CommandSet object must outlive any references obtained via StartHeader<T>() internally (enforced by implementation; callers just pass items).
items may be empty; when empty, nothing is added.

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandSet::Add
functions.description: Convenience method to append a complete header of commands of type T to the CommandSet from a std::vector. If the vector is empty, the call is a no-op. Internally, starts a header for T and adds each (value,index) pair.
requirements: T must be one of: ControlRelayOutputBlock, AnalogOutputInt16, AnalogOutputInt32, AnalogOutputFloat32, or AnalogOutputDouble64.
The CommandSet object must outlive any references obtained via StartHeader<T>() internally (enforced by implementation; callers just pass items).
items may be empty; when empty, nothing is added.

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandSet::StartHeader
functions.description: Begins a new header for commands of type T and returns an ICommandCollection<T>& that allows adding commands (value and index) to this header. This is the generic template; only specific T are supported via explicit specializations.
requirements: T must be one of the explicitly specialized types; otherwise this will be a link/compile-time error.
The returned reference remains valid only as long as the owning CommandSet is alive and not moved from.

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandSet::StartHeader
functions.description: Starts a ControlRelayOutputBlock header and returns a collection interface to add CROB commands to it.
requirements: The returned ICommandCollection<ControlRelayOutputBlock>& must not be used after the CommandSet is destroyed or moved.

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandSet::StartHeader
functions.description: Starts an AnalogOutputInt16 header and returns a collection interface to add AOInt16 commands to it.
requirements: The returned ICommandCollection<AnalogOutputInt16>& must not be used after the CommandSet is destroyed or moved.

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandSet::StartHeader
functions.description: Starts an AnalogOutputInt32 header and returns a collection interface to add AOInt32 commands to it.
requirements: The returned ICommandCollection<AnalogOutputInt32>& must not be used after the CommandSet is destroyed or moved.

functions.name: opendnp3::CommandSet::StartHeader
functions.description: Starts an AnalogOutputFloat32 header and returns a collection interface to add AOFloat32 commands to it.
requirements: The returned ICommandCollection<AnalogOutputFloat32>& must not be used after the CommandSet is destroyed or moved.

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultListenCallbacks::DefaultListenCallbacks
functions.description: Constructor for the default implementation of IListenCallbacks. Creates a listen-callbacks object with default behaviors for accepting connections, certificates, and handling session lifecycle events. Intended to be used when a simple, out-of-the-box policy is sufficient.
requirements: Must be called to instantiate an opendnp3::DefaultListenCallbacks object before it is passed to components that require IListenCallbacks.
No arguments or preconditions are required.

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultListenCallbacks::~DefaultListenCallbacks
functions.description: Virtual destructor for DefaultListenCallbacks. Ensures proper cleanup when the object is destroyed via a base-class (IListenCallbacks) pointer.
requirements: Object must not be used after destruction.
If owned polymorphically through IListenCallbacks*, delete through the base pointer is valid.

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultListenCallbacks::AcceptConnection
functions.signature: virtual bool AcceptConnection(uint64_t sessionid, const std::string& ipaddress) override;
functions.description: Decides whether to accept an incoming connection based on the provided session identifier and peer IP address. Returns true to accept the connection, false to reject. Default behavior is implementation-defined (not shown in this header).
requirements: sessionid: should be the identifier provided by the listening/transport layer for the pending connection (exact semantics unknown; opaque identifier).
ipaddress: caller provides the textual address of the peer (format not specified; typically IPv4/IPv6 string).
Caller should use the boolean return value to proceed (true) or abort (false) the connection establishment.

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultListenCallbacks::AcceptCertificate
functions.signature: virtual bool AcceptCertificate(uint64_t sessionid, const X509Info& info) override;
functions.description: Decides whether to accept a peer's certificate for the given session. Returns true to accept/continue the TLS handshake, false to reject. The X509Info carries certificate details (fields not shown here).
requirements: sessionid must correspond to the active TLS session undergoing certificate validation (opaque identifier; exact semantics unknown).
info must be a valid X509Info structure as supplied by the TLS layer (contents/requirements unknown).
Caller should enforce the return value: true to continue the handshake, false to terminate/reject.

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultListenCallbacks::GetFirstFrameTimeout
functions.description: Returns the time duration to wait for the first DNP3 link-layer frame after a connection is established. Used by the listening stack to bound how long it waits before considering the connection inactive.
requirements: No arguments or caller-side state required.
Caller should honor the returned TimeDuration when configuring or enforcing the first-frame timeout.

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultListenCallbacks::OnFirstFrame
functions.signature: virtual void OnFirstFrame(uint64_t sessionid, const LinkHeaderFields& header, ISessionAcceptor& acceptor) override;
functions.description: Notifies that the first DNP3 link-layer frame has been received on a new connection. Provides the session id, parsed link-layer header fields, and a session acceptor interface the callback can use to accept/establish a master session. Default behavior is implementation-defined.
requirements: sessionid must correspond to the connection on which the first frame was received (opaque identifier).
header must be a valid LinkHeaderFields structure describing the first frame (exact field requirements unknown).
acceptor must be a valid ISessionAcceptor reference for the current connection and remain valid for the duration of the call; the callee may invoke it to accept/create a session.
Caller must ensure this is invoked only once per connection at the time of the first frame reception (implied by method name; exact constraints unknown).

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultListenCallbacks::OnConnectionClose
functions.signature: virtual void OnConnectionClose(uint64_t sessionid, const std::shared_ptr<IMasterSession>& session) override;
functions.description: Notifies that a connection associated with the given session id has been closed. Provides a shared_ptr to the associated IMasterSession, if any, for cleanup or logging. Default behavior is implementation-defined.
requirements: sessionid must be the identifier of the connection that closed (opaque identifier).
session should be the shared_ptr<IMasterSession> associated with the connection; it may be empty/null if no session was established (not specified; treat as unknown).
Caller should invoke this when the transport closes, after any in-flight callbacks related to the same session have completed (exact ordering not specified).

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultListenCallbacks::OnCertificateError
functions.signature: virtual void OnCertificateError(uint64_t sessionid, const X509Info& info, int error) override;
functions.description: Reports a TLS/PKI certificate verification error for a connection. Supplies the session id, the certificate information, and a platform/library-specific error code for diagnostics or policy decisions. Default behavior is implementation-defined.
requirements: sessionid refers to the TLS session where the error occurred (opaque identifier).
info must describe the certificate involved (exact content unknown).
error must be an integer error/status code originating from the TLS/verification layer (semantic mapping unknown).
Caller should invoke this at the time the verification error is detected; any subsequent accept/reject decision must be handled by the TLS pipeline (outside the scope of this callback).

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultMasterApplication::DefaultMasterApplication
functions.description: Default constructor for the DefaultMasterApplication. Creates an instance implementing IMasterApplication with no custom behavior (all callbacks are no-ops except Now()). Intended to be used when an application-specific implementation is not required.
requirements: No arguments; can be default-constructed at any time.
Object must live as long as any callbacks to its methods may occur (if integrated into a stack).

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultMasterApplication::Create
functions.description: Factory method that returns a shared_ptr to a new DefaultMasterApplication instance. Useful for passing an IMasterApplication to APIs expecting a shared pointer.
requirements: Call without arguments; returns a non-null std::shared_ptr.
Caller owns the shared_ptr and is responsible for its lifetime semantics (standard shared ownership).

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultMasterApplication::OnReceiveIIN
functions.description: Callback invoked when an IIN (Internal Indications) field is received from the outstation. The default implementation is a no-op. Applications may override to inspect/act on IIN bits.
requirements: iin must refer to a valid IINField object for the duration of the call.
May be called by the stack thread(s); implementation should be fast and non-blocking if overridden (in this default class it is a no-op).

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultMasterApplication::OnTaskStart
functions.description: Callback when a master task starts (e.g., scans, integrity polls). Default implementation is a no-op.
requirements: type and id values are provided by the stack; callers typically should not invoke this directly.
If overridden, implementation should be thread-safe and non-blocking. In this default class it is a no-op.

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultMasterApplication::OnTaskComplete
functions.description: Callback when a master task completes, with details in TaskInfo. Default implementation is a no-op.
requirements: info must refer to a valid TaskInfo object for the duration of the call.
If overridden, implementation should be thread-safe and non-blocking. In this default class it is a no-op.

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultMasterApplication::AssignClassDuringStartup
functions.description: Indicates whether the master should perform a Class Assignment request during startup. Default returns false, meaning no class assignment will be attempted.
requirements: No arguments. Return value controls whether the stack initiates class assignment at startup.
If overridden in a subclass, callers should expect true to trigger configuration of an assign-class request via ConfigureAssignClassRequest.

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultMasterApplication::ConfigureAssignClassRequest
functions.description: Provides a callback to populate an Assign Class request when AssignClassDuringStartup() returns true. Default implementation is a no-op (adds no headers).
requirements: fun must be a valid callable (as defined by WriteHeaderFunT) for the duration of the call; it will be invoked to write request headers.
This function is expected to be called by the stack only if AssignClassDuringStartup() returns true.
In this default class, nothing is written; overriding implementations should only call fun with valid header parameters.

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultMasterApplication::Now
functions.description: Returns the current UTC timestamp for time-stamping operations. The exact source of time is not shown in this header; typical implementations return the system wall clock in UTC.
requirements: No arguments. Must return a valid UTCTimestamp value.
Actual behavior depends on implementation elsewhere; callers should not assume high-precision or monotonicity beyond what UTCTimestamp guarantees (details unknown from this header).

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultMasterApplication::OnStateChange
functions.description: Callback when the link layer status changes. Default implementation is a no-op.
requirements: value must be a valid LinkStatus enumerator.
If overridden, implementation should be thread-safe and non-blocking. In this default class it is a no-op.

functions.name: opendnp3::Header::WriteTo
functions.description: Writes the configured DNP3 object header to the provided HeaderWriter. Intended to serialize the Header into a request/response being built by the writer. functions.name: opendnp3::ICommandCollection::Add
functions.signature: virtual opendnp3::ICommandCollection<T>& Add(const T& command, uint16_t index) = 0;
functions.description: Adds a command of type T to the collection at the specified 16-bit index. This is a pure virtual interface method; concrete implementations define how commands are stored or scheduled. The return value is a reference to the collection, enabling call chaining. Usage: obtain a concrete ICommandCollection<T> from the library and call Add(cmd, idx) for each command to enqueue.
requirements: Must be invoked on a valid concrete instance of opendnp3::ICommandCollection<T> (this is a pure virtual interface).
Template parameter T must match the collection’s concrete type; the command argument must be a valid const T reference.
index must be within the range of uint16_t (0 to 65535).
The command object must be in a state acceptable to the implementation (details unknown due to interface-only declaration).
Error handling semantics (e.g., failure conditions, exceptions, or return codes) are implementation-defined and not specified in this header.

functions.name: opendnp3::ICommandProcessor::SelectAndOperate
functions.signature: virtual void opendnp3::ICommandProcessor::SelectAndOperate(opendnp3::CommandSet&& commands, const opendnp3::CommandResultCallbackT& callback, const opendnp3::TaskConfig& config = opendnp3::TaskConfig::Default()) = 0;
functions.description: Dispatches a DNP3 Select-and-Operate sequence for a set of command headers to the master. The operation is asynchronous; the provided callback is invoked upon completion or failure. Use this when you want a two-step Select/Operate semantics enforced by the stack. The TaskConfig may be used to control normal callbacks and specify the user for Secure Authentication (SA).
requirements: commands must be a valid set of command headers appropriate for the target outstation (content-specific validity is application/domain dependent).
commands is consumed by move; pass an rvalue (e.g., std::move) as required by the CommandSet&& parameter.
callback must be a valid callable and remain valid until the stack invokes it upon completion or failure.
config, if provided, must have been initialized via opendnp3::TaskConfig and may influence callback behavior and SA user selection.
Function is pure virtual; a concrete implementation of ICommandProcessor must be used.

functions.name: opendnp3::ICommandProcessor::DirectOperate

functions.description: Dispatches a DNP3 Direct-Operate for a set of command headers to the master. The operation is asynchronous; the provided callback is invoked upon completion or failure. Use this to bypass Select and issue a direct operation. The TaskConfig may be used to control normal callbacks and specify the user for Secure Authentication (SA).
requirements: commands must be a valid set of command headers appropriate for the target outstation (content-specific validity is application/domain dependent).
commands is consumed by move; pass an rvalue (e.g., std::move) as required by the CommandSet&& parameter.
callback must be a valid callable and remain valid until the stack invokes it upon completion or failure.
config, if provided, must have been initialized via opendnp3::TaskConfig and may influence callback behavior and SA user selection.
Function is pure virtual; a concrete implementation of ICommandProcessor must be used.

functions.signature:

void opendnp3::ICommandProcessor::SelectAndOperate(const T& command, uint16_t index, const opendnp3::CommandResultCallbackT& callback, const opendnp3::TaskConfig& config = opendnp3::TaskConfig::Default());
functions.description: Convenience template that performs a Select-and-Operate for a single command value T at the specified index. Internally wraps the command with its index (WithIndex) into a CommandSet and forwards to the virtual SelectAndOperate. Asynchronous; the callback is invoked upon completion or failure.
requirements: T must be a command type compatible with opendnp3::WithIndex and opendnp3::CommandSet (e.g., a supported DNP3 command type).
index is a 16-bit point index; valid range is 0..65535 due to the uint16_t type.
callback must be a valid callable and remain valid until invocation.
config, if provided, must be a valid opendnp3::TaskConfig.
The ICommandProcessor instance must be a valid concrete implementation since this forwards to the virtual SelectAndOperate.

requirements: T must be a command type compatible with opendnp3::WithIndex and opendnp3::CommandSet (e.g., a supported DNP3 command type).

callback must be a valid callable and remain valid until invocation.

The ICommandProcessor instance must be a valid concrete implementation since this forwards to the virtual DirectOperate.

Implementations should create (or otherwise provide) and return a new IMasterSession bound to the supplied handlers and configuration, or handle the acceptance according to application policy. Typical usage: the DNP3 stack or server calls this method on an ISessionAcceptor to establish a master session for an incoming connection identified by sessionid. Detailed acceptance criteria and ownership semantics beyond the shared_ptr interfaces are not specified in this header.
requirements: Must be implemented by concrete subclasses (pure virtual).
The caller must pass a valid std::string sessionid; format and uniqueness are not specified (unknown).

The caller must pass valid (non-expired) std::shared_ptr instances for SOEHandler and application; they must remain valid for the duration of the call. Further lifetime guarantees beyond the call are unspecified (unknown).

The caller must provide a valid opendnp3::MasterStackConfig object; it must remain valid for the duration of the call. Specific field requirements within MasterStackConfig are not specified here (unknown).
Return value is a std::shared_ptr<IMasterSession>; whether nullptr is permitted to indicate rejection is not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: opendnp3::ISOEHandler::~ISOEHandler
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the ISOEHandler interface. Allows derived classes to clean up resources when an instance is destroyed. Typically invoked by the DNP3 stack or application code holding a base pointer.
requirements: No arguments or preconditions.

functions.name: opendnp3::ISOEHandler::BeginFragment
functions.description: Callback invoked at the start of a response fragment received by the master stack. Use this to prepare state before processing contained measurements/events. The ResponseInfo describes the fragment context.
requirements: info must refer to a valid opendnp3::ResponseInfo object for the current fragment (inferred from const reference).
May be called before any Process(...) callbacks for the same fragment (implied by name and typical usage).

functions.name: opendnp3::ISOEHandler::EndFragment
functions.description: Callback invoked at the end of a response fragment. Use this to finalize any per-fragment processing after all contained values have been delivered. The ResponseInfo describes the fragment context.
requirements: info must refer to a valid opendnp3::ResponseInfo object for the current fragment (inferred from const reference).
Typically called after all corresponding Process(...) calls for the fragment (implied by name and typical usage).

functions.name: opendnp3::ISOEHandler::Process
functions.signature: virtual void opendnp3::ISOEHandler::Process(const opendnp3::HeaderInfo& info, const opendnp3::ICollection<opendnp3::Indexed<opendnp3::Binary>>& values) = 0
functions.description: Processes a collection of Binary measurements reported in a response ASDU. HeaderInfo describes the associated object header.
requirements: info must be a valid reference describing the header for the provided values (inferred from const reference and comment).

functions.name: opendnp3::ITaskCallback::OnStart
functions.description: Indicates that the associated task has begun running. This is a pure virtual callback method to be implemented by users of ITaskCallback. Typical usage: the DNP3 stack/framework invokes this on the callback object when a task transitions to the running state; implementations may record state, start timing, or update diagnostics. Additional behavioral details (threading, timing guarantees) are unknown from this header.
requirements: Must be implemented by a concrete subclass of opendnp3::ITaskCallback (pure virtual).
Caller should only invoke this when the task actually starts, as per the comment.
No invocation of this method should occur after OnDestroyed() has been called on the same callback instance.
No argument or return value constraints apply; there is no return value and no parameters.
Threading and reentrancy requirements are unknown from this header.

functions.name: opendnp3::ITaskCallback::OnComplete
functions.description: Notifies that the task has completed, either successfully or with failure. This pure virtual callback is invoked by the framework with a TaskCompletion result code. Implementations typically use the result to log outcomes, trigger follow-up actions, or update state. Exact ordering beyond start/complete and any threading guarantees are unknown from this header.
requirements: Must be implemented by a concrete subclass of opendnp3::ITaskCallback (pure virtual).
Caller must pass a valid opendnp3::TaskCompletion value in 'result'.
Caller should invoke this upon task completion (success or failure), as per the comment.
No invocation of this method should occur after OnDestroyed() has been called on the same callback instance.
No specific guarantee is stated about being called exactly once; multiplicity constraints are unknown from this header.
Error handling behavior (exceptions allowed or not) is unknown from this header.

functions.name: opendnp3::ITaskCallback::OnDestroyed
functions.description: Signals that the task is being destroyed and no further OnStart/OnComplete callbacks will occur. This pure virtual callback allows implementations to release resources or finalize state tied to the task lifecycle. Further behavioral details (e.g., who calls it and on which thread) are unknown from this header.
requirements: Must be implemented by a concrete subclass of opendnp3::ITaskCallback (pure virtual).
Caller should only invoke this when the task no longer exists and no more calls will be made to OnStart or OnComplete, as stated in the comment.
After OnDestroyed() is invoked for a given callback instance, the caller must not call OnStart() or OnComplete() again on that instance.
No parameters or return value constraints apply.
Timing and threading guarantees are unknown from this header.

functions.name: opendnp3::IUTCTimeSource::Now
functions.description: Returns a UTCTimestamp representing the current time. This is a pure virtual method on the opendnp3::IUTCTimeSource interface that implementations must override to supply a UTC timestamp source. Typical usage: obtain a concrete IUTCTimeSource implementation and call Now() to retrieve the current UTC timestamp. Notes: the method is not const-qualified; no guarantees about monotonicity, precision, or error handling are documented.
requirements: Must be invoked on a valid, concrete implementation of opendnp3::IUTCTimeSource (the interface itself is abstract).
Caller must have non-const access to the IUTCTimeSource instance (method is not const-qualified).
No arguments are required; no additional preconditions are documented.

functions.name: opendnp3::PrintingSOEHandler::Create
functions.description: Factory method that creates a shared instance of a PrintingSOEHandler returned as an ISOEHandler. Intended for users who want an ISOEHandler implementation that prints received SOE data to std::cout.

functions.name: opendnp3::PrintingSOEHandler::BeginFragment
functions.description: Notification invoked at the start of processing a DNP3 response fragment. In this implementation it will print fragment metadata to the console (exact formatting not shown here). Use as part of the ISOEHandler callback sequence.

functions.name: opendnp3::PrintingSOEHandler::EndFragment
functions.description: Notification invoked at the end of processing a DNP3 response fragment. This implementation prints closing/summary information to the console (exact formatting not shown here).

values must be a valid collection with ForeachItem iteration.

requirements: info must be valid opendnp3::HeaderInfo.

functions.description: Processes a collection of indexed TimeAndInterval measurements and prints index, value (via operator<<), flags, and timestamp to std::cout.
requirements: info must be valid opendnp3::HeaderInfo.

Side effects: writes to std::cout.

functions.name: opendnp3::TaskConfig::TaskConfig
functions.description: Constructs a TaskConfig with an explicit TaskId and optional ITaskCallback. Use this to associate a specific TaskId and an optional callback with a task configuration. Note: the default (no-arg) constructor is deleted; use this constructor or the static factory helpers.
requirements: taskId must be a valid opendnp3::TaskId value; TaskId::Undefined() is allowed.
pCallback may be null or a valid std::shared_ptr to an object implementing opendnp3::ITaskCallback.
The deleted default constructor means callers must not attempt to default-construct TaskConfig.

functions.name: opendnp3::TaskConfig::Default
functions.description: Creates a TaskConfig with TaskId::Undefined() and no callback (nullptr). Useful as a baseline configuration when no explicit TaskId or callback is required.
requirements: No arguments required.
Returns a value-initialized TaskConfig with TaskId::Undefined() and pCallback == nullptr.

functions.name: opendnp3::TaskConfig::With
functions.description: Creates a TaskConfig with TaskId::Undefined() and an optional ITaskCallback. Use this helper when only a callback needs to be supplied and the TaskId can remain undefined.
requirements: callback may be null or a valid std::shared_ptr to an object implementing opendnp3::ITaskCallback.
Resulting TaskConfig will have TaskId::Undefined().

functions.name: opendnp3::TaskId::Defined
functions.description: Factory method that constructs a defined TaskId with the supplied integer identifier. Use this to create a valid task identifier handle. The exact valid range/semantics of id are not documented here; -1 appears reserved internally for undefined based on the class implementation. If you later need the numeric id, call GetId(); check IsDefined() to distinguish defined vs. undefined handles.
requirements: Must supply an integer id (no specific range documented).
The returned TaskId is value-type and can be copied/moved freely (implied by structure).
Caller should not assume any special meaning beyond being an identifier; check IsDefined() if differentiating from undefined is required (inferred from API).

functions.name: opendnp3::TaskId::Undefined
functions.description: Factory method that constructs an undefined TaskId sentinel. Use this when no valid task identifier is available or to represent the absence of a running task. The internal id is set to a sentinel value (-1) and IsDefined() will return false.
requirements: No arguments required.
The returned TaskId represents an undefined/invalid handle; callers should check IsDefined() before using GetId() for meaningful logic (inferred from API).

functions.name: opendnp3::TaskId::GetId
functions.description: Returns the underlying integer identifier associated with this TaskId. Typically used after confirming the TaskId is defined via IsDefined(). If the TaskId is undefined, the value may be a sentinel (-1) based on the implementation.
requirements: The TaskId instance must be initialized (constructed via Defined() or Undefined()).
For meaningful identifiers, callers should ensure IsDefined() returns true before using the returned value (inferred from API).

functions.name: opendnp3::TaskId::IsDefined
functions.description: Indicates whether this TaskId represents a defined (valid) task identifier. Use this to distinguish valid identifiers from the undefined sentinel created by Undefined().
requirements: The TaskId instance must be initialized (constructed via Defined() or Undefined()).

functions.name: opendnp3::TaskInfo::TaskInfo
functions.description: Constructs a TaskInfo object that records the type of a master task, its completion result, and the task identifier. Intended to be used to report or propagate the outcome of a completed or failed master task. The constructor simply initializes the public members (type, result, id) with the provided values; no additional logic is performed.
requirements: type_ must be a valid opendnp3::MasterTaskType enumerator.
result_ must be a valid opendnp3::TaskCompletion enumerator representing the task’s completion status.
id_ must be an initialized opendnp3::TaskId value identifying the task (no specific format or constraints are documented in this header).

functions.name: opendnp3::ApplicationIIN::ApplicationIIN
functions.description: Default constructor for ApplicationIIN. Initializes all application-controlled IIN flags (needTime, localControl, deviceTrouble, configCorrupt, eventBufferOverflow) to false. Use this to create an instance and then set the desired flags before converting to an IINField.
requirements: No arguments are required.
Constructed object’s flags default to false; callers should explicitly set any flags they need before further use.
No side effects beyond initializing member fields.

functions.name: opendnp3::ApplicationIIN::ToIIN
functions.description: Builds and returns an IINField representing the current state of the application-controlled IIN bits. Intended to be called by the outstation application to translate the ApplicationIIN boolean flags (needTime, localControl, deviceTrouble, configCorrupt, and eventBufferOverflow) into the bitfield used on the wire.
requirements: The ApplicationIIN instance should have its flags set to the desired values before calling.
Function is const and does not modify the object.
Requires opendnp3/app/IINField.h to be available at compile time (type dependency).
Exact bit-to-flag mapping is not specified in this header; callers should rely on library semantics of IINField for interpretation.

functions.name: opendnp3::DatabaseConfig::DatabaseConfig
functions.description: Default constructor for DatabaseConfig. Creates an instance with all configuration maps default-constructed and empty so callers can populate per-index MeasurementConfig entries as needed.
requirements: No arguments required.

Resulting maps (binary_input, double_binary, analog_input, counter, frozen_counter, binary_output_status, analog_output_status, time_and_interval, octet_string) are empty and should be populated by the caller as appropriate before use.
Caller must include opendnp3/outstation/MeasurementConfig.h and construct within the opendnp3 namespace context or with qualified names.

functions.name: opendnp3::DatabaseConfig::DatabaseConfig
functions.description: Constructs a DatabaseConfig possibly initializing configuration for all point types based on a single count parameter. The header does not define behavior; typical usage in opendnp3 suggests this may allocate or pre-populate default configurations for each measurement type up to the given count, but exact initialization details are unknown from this file.
requirements: Parameter all_types is a 16-bit unsigned integer; valid range is 0..65535 by type, exact semantic meaning is not specified in this header.
No other preconditions are stated; callers should not assume specific map sizes or contents without consulting the implementation or higher-level documentation.
If relying on this constructor to populate maps, verify behavior in the corresponding source or documentation; otherwise, be prepared to explicitly fill the maps after construction.

functions.description: Constructor for the default outstation application. Initializes the instance with a configurable time synchronization refresh rate used internally for time validity/refresh checks.

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultOutstationApplication::SupportsWriteAbsoluteTime

Return value semantics beyond success/failure are not documented here (unknown specifics).

functions.description: Indicates whether the outstation supports writing time-and-interval objects. This default implementation reports no support (returns false).

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultOutstationApplication::SupportsAssignClass
functions.description: Indicates whether the outstation supports class assignment. This default implementation reports support (returns true).

start, stop: numeric range semantics not documented here (unknown specifics).

functions.description: Indicates the outstation’s warm restart capability. This default implementation reports unsupported.

functions.name: opendnp3::DefaultOutstationApplication::WarmRestart
functions.description: Requests a warm restart and returns the restart delay in seconds if supported. This default implementation returns the special value 65535, typically indicating unsupported/unknown delay.
requirements: No arguments. Always returns 65535 in this implementation.

functions.name: opendnp3::EventBufferConfig::AllTypes
functions.description: Factory function that creates an EventBufferConfig where every event category shares the same maximum count specified by sizes. Intended mainly for demos or systems that produce all event types uniformly. Use when you want a uniform buffer capacity across all event types; the total preallocated buffer size is proportional to the sum across all types.
requirements: sizes is a count and must be representable by uint16_t (0..65535).

The resulting total buffer size (sum across all event types) determines the size of the preallocated heap buffer; callers should choose sizes appropriate to memory constraints and expected polling frequency.

functions.name: opendnp3::EventBufferConfig::EventBufferConfig
functions.signature: opendnp3::EventBufferConfig::EventBufferConfig(uint16_t maxBinaryEvents = 0, uint16_t maxDoubleBinaryEvents = 0, uint16_t maxAnalogEvents = 0, uint16_t maxCounterEvents = 0, uint16_t maxFrozenCounterEvents = 0, uint16_t maxBinaryOutputStatusEvents = 0, uint16_t maxAnalogOutputStatusEvents = 0, uint16_t maxOctetStringEvents = 0);
functions.description: Constructor that initializes per-type maximum event counts for the outstation’s event buffer. Use this to fine-tune how many events of each DNP3 type are retained before overflow. The implementation uses a preallocated heap buffer whose size is proportional to the sum of these maxima.
requirements: Each argument is a non-negative count representable by uint16_t (0..65535).
The sum of all per-type maxima determines the preallocated heap buffer size; callers should select values consistent with available memory and expected event rates/polling frequency.

functions.name: opendnp3::EventBufferConfig::TotalEvents
functions.description: Returns the total number of events that can be stored across all types, i.e., the sum of all per-type maximums. This value correlates directly to the number of elements in the preallocated event buffer.
requirements: The EventBufferConfig instance must be initialized (constructed) before calling.
No side effects; callable at any time to query capacity.

functions.name: opendnp3::ICommandHandler::~ICommandHandler
functions.description: Virtual destructor for ICommandHandler allowing safe deletion via a base-class pointer. Defaulted implementation; no operational behavior.

functions.name: opendnp3::ICommandHandler::Begin
functions.description: Marks the start of processing a command APDU. Called by the outstation framework before one or more Select/Operate/DIRECT OPERATE requests are dispatched.

Intended to be called by the outstation command-processing framework; external callers should not invoke unless implementing equivalent sequencing.
Any internal state established here must be valid until End() is called.

functions.name: opendnp3::ICommandHandler::End
functions.description: Marks the end of processing a command APDU. Completes the transaction started by Begin().
requirements: Should be called exactly once after a matching Begin() to close the command-processing window (per comment intent).
Intended to be called by the outstation command-processing framework; external callers should not invoke unless implementing equivalent sequencing.
Any resources or transactional state set up in Begin() should be finalized or released here.

functions.name: opendnp3::ICommandHandler::Select
functions.signature: virtual CommandStatus Select(const ControlRelayOutputBlock& command, uint16_t index) = 0;
functions.description: Query whether a ControlRelayOutputBlock (G12V1) at the specified index is supported/acceptable. Used during DNP3 SELECT phase prior to OPERATE.
requirements: command must be a valid ControlRelayOutputBlock instance; its fields should reflect the intended control action.
index identifies the target point; it should refer to a valid outstation/control point index (exact range unknown; determined by application configuration).
Return value (CommandStatus) communicates acceptance/rejection and must be honored by the caller when deciding whether to proceed to Operate. (DNP3 pattern; inferred).

functions.name: opendnp3::ICommandHandler::Operate
functions.signature: virtual CommandStatus Operate(const ControlRelayOutputBlock& command, uint16_t index, IUpdateHandler& handler, OperateType opType) = 0;
functions.description: Execute a ControlRelayOutputBlock (G12V1) control at the specified index. The supplied IUpdateHandler can be used to load resulting measurement/state changes. opType reflects the received operation type (e.g., SelectBeforeOperate vs. DirectOperate).
requirements: command must be a valid ControlRelayOutputBlock describing the desired control.
index must identify a valid control point (exact range unknown; application-defined).
handler must be a valid reference for the duration of the call; implementers may use it to report updates resulting from the operation.
opType must match the operation the outstation received; callers should pass the correct OperateType provided by the protocol layer.
Typically called only after a successful Select for the same point and parameters when using Select-Before-Operate. (Inferred from DNP3 semantics).
Return CommandStatus must be checked by the caller to handle success/failure.

functions.name: opendnp3::IDnpTimeSource::Now
functions.description: Returns a DNPTime representing the current time, intended for use when freezing counters. This is a virtual method on IDnpTimeSource and can be overridden by derived classes to supply a real time source. The default implementation returns a timestamp of 0 with TimestampQuality::INVALID, indicating no valid time is available. Typical usage is to call Now() at the moment a freeze operation (or similar time-stamping action) occurs and then propagate the returned DNPTime to downstream logic that requires a timestamp.
requirements: Callers must not assume the returned timestamp is valid; they should check the DNPTime quality field (e.g., handle TimestampQuality::INVALID).
If accurate current time is required, the provided instance should be of a type that overrides Now() to supply a valid timestamp (the base implementation returns an invalid timestamp).
Object must be a valid, live instance of opendnp3::IDnpTimeSource (or a derived type) when calling the method; reentrancy/thread-safety characteristics are not specified.

functions.name: opendnp3::IOutstation::~IOutstation

Call through a pointer/reference to a derived implementation; destructor is virtual to support polymorphic deletion.

functions.name: opendnp3::IOutstation::SetLogFilters
functions.description: Adjusts the outstation’s logging configuration to the specified filter levels. Intended for runtime reconfiguration of what the outstation logs.

functions.description: Sets the outstation’s Restart IIN bit. The comment indicates this is mainly for simulating restarts and typically should not be used in normal applications.

functions.description: Applies a batch of measurement updates to the outstation. Use to push a prepared set of values (Updates) into the running outstation.

functions.name: opendnp3::IOutstationApplication::SupportsWriteAbsoluteTime
functions.description: Indicates whether the outstation application supports absolute time writes. If false, WriteAbsoluteTime will never be invoked and the outstation will respond with IIN 2.1 (FUNC_NOT_SUPPORTED) to such requests.
requirements: No arguments; simply return true to enable WriteAbsoluteTime callbacks, false to disable them.
If this returns false, callers must not invoke WriteAbsoluteTime on this instance (the stack won’t).

functions.name: opendnp3::IOutstationApplication::WriteAbsoluteTime
functions.description: Attempts to write an absolute time value to the outstation. Only called if SupportsWriteAbsoluteTime() returns true. Returning true accepts the time; returning false causes the outstation to set IIN 2.3 (PARAM_ERROR). Implementations should clear the NEED_TIME field when handling this write.

import random
import string
from typing import List

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Mix of printable ASCII plus a few punctuation likely used in tokens
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _choice(r: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[r.randrange(len(items))]

# Curated corpus of interesting valid tokens and typical values used across stubs
_CANON_TOKENS = [

    "CONFIRM","READ","WRITE","SELECT","OPERATE","DIRECT_OPERATE","DIRECT_OPERATE_NR",
    "ENABLE_UNSOLICITED","DISABLE_UNSOLICITED","ASSIGN_CLASS","RESPONSE","UNSOLICITED_RESPONSE",

    "Group1Var2","Group2Var2","Group32Var5","Group32Var6","Group32Var7","Group32Var8",

# Additional payload strings useful for logging
_LOG_IDS = [
    "master-1","outstation-1","session-abc","chan/tcp:127.0.0.1:20000","tls:example.com:20000",
    "αβγ-logger","日本語logger","id_with_underscores","prod|eu-west-1","dev:test:logger"
]

_MESSAGES = [
    "hello world","quick brown fox","lorem ipsum dolor sit amet","state change observed",
    "handshake complete","connection failed: timeout","parsing canonical token",
    "performing integrity poll","event buffer overflow detected","retry backoff triggered"
]

_LOCATIONS = [
    "File.cpp:123","Module/Decoder.cpp:45","Logger.hpp:210","IListenCallbacks.cc:78",
    "Outstation.cpp:512","MasterOps.cpp:33","main.cc:1","unknown:0"
]

# For OctetString cases, include some lengths near edges
_OCTET_PATTERNS = [
    "\x00", # minimal default-like
    "\x01\x02\x03",
    "A" * 10,
    "B" * 254,
    "C" * 255,
]

# Build a single buffer containing multiple newline-separated strings so FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls
# in the harness consume meaningful values in sequence.

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[str] = []

    # 1) Provide several enum tokens likely to be parsed by *::from_string stubs
    # Mix valid tokens and random strings to exercise both paths (but keep valid majority)
    for _ in range(10):
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            parts.append(_choice(r, _CANON_TOKENS))
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 24))

    # 2) Provide logger ids, locations, and messages used by ConsoleLogger/Logger stubs
    for _ in range(3):
        parts.append(_choice(r, _LOG_IDS))
    for _ in range(3):
        parts.append(_choice(r, _LOCATIONS))
    for _ in range(5):
        # Some messages longer to test truncation paths
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(_choice(r, _MESSAGES))
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 50, 200))

    # 3) Include plausible IP addresses / hostnames for IPEndpoint and AcceptConnection
    ip_octets = [str(r.randrange(0,256)) for _ in range(4)]
    parts.append(".".join(ip_octets))
    parts.append("127.0.0.1")
    parts.append("0.0.0.0")
    parts.append("localhost")
    parts.append("example.com")

    # 4) Include some OctetString-friendly raw sequences represented as escaped sequences
    parts.extend(_OCTET_PATTERNS)

    # 5) Add some more group/variation tokens and miscellaneous identifiers
    parts.extend([
        "Group42Var3","Group41Var2","Group11Var1","Group22Var6",
        "session-" + _rand_ascii(r, 4, 8),
        "scan-interval-" + str(r.randint(1, 60)) + "s",
    ])

    # 6) Pad with additional random strings to satisfy any extra FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls
    for _ in range(20):
        parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 64))

    # Join with newlines, since most fuzz harnesses split on NUL or newline; use newline to preserve C-string property
    data = "\n".join(parts).encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

    # Ensure maximum size limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# We generate interesting raw byte sequences suitable for:
# - opendnp3::Buffer feeds to Decoder::Decode{LPDU,TPDU,APDU}
# - Strings used by OctetData constructors and Set(), and X509Info subject/thumbprint
# The fuzzer obtains data via FUZZ_PARAM_STR and integers; we only control the initial
# input buffer. We'll pack multiple self-describing blobs so different FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls
# can consume distinct slices while remaining valid. We avoid mutations and aim for valid yet
# diverse payloads.

# Format of the generated buffer:
# [u16 count][chunks...]
# each chunk = [u16 len][u8 type][len bytes payload]
# types:
#  0 = printable ASCII string (for c_str paths)
#  1 = binary octets length 0..255 typical (for OctetData small)
#  2 = larger binary up to ~1024 (for Decoder buffers)
#  3 = UTF-8 like subject names
#  4 = mixed bytes including zeros (for edge cases)
# Consumers in fuzz stubs will call FUZZ_PARAM_STR repeatedly; many harnesses pop sequentially.
# We thus concatenate multiple chunk payloads back-to-back, so each call gets the next slice.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_- .:/\\@#%+*()[]{}|," \
               b"\t\r\n"
    return bytes(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_utf8ish(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.7:
            out.append(r.randint(0x20, 0x7E))
        elif choice < 0.85:
            # 2-byte UTF-8
            cp = r.randint(0x80, 0x7FF)
            out.append(0xC0 | (cp >> 6))
            out.append(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F))
        elif choice < 0.95:
            # 3-byte
            cp = r.randint(0x800, 0xFFFF)
            out.append(0xE0 | (cp >> 12))
            out.append(0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F))
            out.append(0x80 | (cp & 0x3F))
        else:
            # nulls
            out.append(0)
    return bytes(out[:n])

def _rand_binary(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return r.randbytes(n)

def _lpdu_like(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build something resembling a DNP3 link-layer frame to hit more decoder paths.
    # DNP3 link header: 0x05 0x64 LEN CTRL DEST_L DEST_H SRC_L SRC_H CRC_L CRC_H ...
    # We'll make a plausible frame with random payload and placeholder CRCs.
    payload_len = r.randint(0, max(0, max_len - 10))
    ctrl = r.randint(0, 0xFF)
    dest = r.randint(0, 0xFFFF)
    src = r.randint(0, 0xFFFF)
    length = 5 + payload_len  # 5 bytes after LEN before first CRC
    header = bytearray([0x05, 0x64, length & 0xFF, ctrl, dest & 0xFF, (dest >> 8) & 0xFF,
                        src & 0xFF, (src >> 8) & 0xFF])
    data = r.randbytes(payload_len)
    # Append fake CRCs (two bytes) – decoder should tolerate errors.
    frame = header + data + bytes([r.randint(0, 255), r.randint(0, 255)])
    return bytes(frame[:max_len])

def _build_chunks(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    # Mix of chunks to satisfy multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers
    # 1) Nice ASCII id/string
    chunks.append(_rand_ascii(r, 0, 64))
    # 2) small octet (<=255) with possible zero length to test default [0x00]
    small_len = r.choice([0, r.randint(1, 255)])
    chunks.append(bytes([0]) * small_len if r.random() < 0.3 else _rand_binary(r, small_len, small_len))
    # 3) medium binary for TPDU/APDU
    chunks.append(_rand_binary(r, 0, 512))
    # 4) UTF-8 subject-like
    chunks.append(_rand_utf8ish(r, 0, 128))
    # 5) LPDU-like frame
    chunks.append(_lpdu_like(r, r.randint(10, 512)))
    # 6) Another ASCII
    chunks.append(_rand_ascii(r, 0, 256))
    # 7) Another binary with embedded zeros
    b = bytearray(_rand_binary(r, 0, 512))
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 8)):
        if len(b) == 0:
            break
        b[r.randrange(len(b))] = 0
    chunks.append(bytes(b))
    return chunks

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    chunks = _build_chunks(r)
    # Serialize as simple concatenation without headers since FUZZ_PARAM_STR likely pulls slices sequentially.
    # However, to diversify early consumption, interleave sizes and data so substring boundaries align.
    out = bytearray()
    for payload in chunks:
        # prefix with a 2-byte length to allow consumers that read variable amounts to get bounded slices
        out += struct.pack('<H', len(payload))
        out += payload
    # Ensure size limit
    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() and FUZZ_PARAM_STR() used by the TLSConfig fuzzer.
# We aim to provide a small virtual filesystem layout encoded in a single byte buffer that the fuzzer
# runtime will materialize as files and strings. The format here follows common AFL-style multi-part
# buffers where filenames and file contents are embedded sequentially.
#
# Strategy:
# - Create 1–3 PEM-like files with realistic names and contents:
#   - a CA/peer certificate file
#   - a local certificate chain file
#   - a private key file (sometimes identical path as local cert to exercise combined PEM handling)
# - Include realistic PEM markers, a mix of RSA/ECDSA headers, and plausible cipher list strings.
# - Provide random booleans packed as integers for TLS version flags and chooser bit.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Buffer layout (simple, self-describing):
#   magic: 4 bytes b"TLSG"
#   count: 1 byte number of file entries (1..3)
#   For each file entry:
#     name_len: 1 byte
#     name: name_len bytes (UTF-8)
#     content_len: 2 bytes little-endian (<= 1500)
#     content: content_len bytes
#   Section: parameters
#     chooser_uint32: 4 bytes (LSB decides if private key path == local cert path)
#     tlsflags1_uint32: 4 bytes (bitfield for v10)
#     tlsflags2_uint32: 4 bytes (bitfield for v11)
#     tlsflags3_uint32: 4 bytes (bitfield for v12)
#     tlsflags4_uint32: 4 bytes (bitfield for v13)
#   Cipher list string:
#     clen: 2 bytes little-endian
#     cstr: clen bytes (ASCII)
#
# The fuzzer harness typically maps FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() to successive file names from the buffer
# and FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to the cipher list string we include.

PEM_CERT_BLOCKS = [
    ("CERTIFICATE", "MIICdzCCAeCgAwIBAgIBADANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQsFADA"),
    ("CERTIFICATE", "MIIBezCCASGgAwIBAgIURjIXYw9s5i...snip...HwIDAQAB"),
]

PEM_KEY_BLOCKS = [
    ("RSA PRIVATE KEY", "MIIEpAIBAAKCAQEAu1k...snip...IDAQAB"),
    ("EC PRIVATE KEY", "MHcCAQEEIF3R...snip...ZtR6Q=="),
]

PEM_CHAIN_EXTRA = (
    "CERTIFICATE",
    "MIIDeDCCAmCgAwIBAgIUXy...snip...ABCD"
)

CIPHER_LISTS = [
    b"",  # empty -> default
    b"DEFAULT:@SECLEVEL=1",
    b"HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5",
    b"TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256",
    b"ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305",
]

FILENAMES = [
    b"peer_ca.pem",
    b"local_cert.pem",
    b"private_key.pem",
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _pem_block(kind: str, body_base64: str) -> bytes:
    # Compose a minimal PEM with headers/footers and line breaks
    header = f"-----BEGIN {kind}-----\n"
    footer = f"-----END {kind}-----\n"
    # Insert line breaks to look realistic
    body = body_base64
    lines = [body[i:i+64] for i in range(0, len(body), 64)]
    pem = header + "\n".join(lines) + "\n" + footer
    return pem.encode("ascii")


def _make_cert_pem(rng: random.Random, chain: bool) -> bytes:
    # Primary cert
    kind, b64 = rng.choice(PEM_CERT_BLOCKS)
    parts = [_pem_block(kind, b64)]
    # Optionally add extra cert to emulate chain
    if chain:
        ekind, eb64 = PEM_CHAIN_EXTRA
        parts.append(_pem_block(ekind, eb64))
    return b"".join(parts)


def _make_key_pem(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    kind, b64 = rng.choice(PEM_KEY_BLOCKS)
    return _pem_block(kind, b64)


def _bounded(u: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return max(lo, min(hi, u))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide how many files (always provide at least the two cert files). Sometimes provide 3rd key file.
    provide_key = rng.choice([True, False])
    count = 3 if provide_key else 2

    # Build contents
    peer_cert = _make_cert_pem(rng, chain=False)
    local_cert_chain = _make_cert_pem(rng, chain=True)

    # In some cases, key is same as local cert to exercise combined PEM
    same_file = rng.choice([True, False])
    private_key = local_cert_chain if same_file else _make_key_pem(rng)

    # Construct chooser and TLS flags (uint32), keeping variability but deterministic by seed
    chooser = 1 if same_file else 0
    # Use random patterns but ensure v12/v13 are often enabled (set bits frequently)
    flags = []
    for i in range(4):
        val = rng.getrandbits(32)
        if i >= 2:  # v12/v13
            val |= 0x1  # ensure non-zero so occasionally true when masked in stub
        flags.append(val)

    # Choose cipher list (sometimes empty to keep defaults)
    cipher = rng.choice(CIPHER_LISTS)
    # Occasionally produce a custom cipher string with plausible tokens
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        tokens = [
            b"HIGH", b"MEDIUM", b"@SECLEVEL=2", b"!aNULL", b"!eNULL", b"!MD5",
            b"TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256", b"TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384", b"TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256",
            b"ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256", b"ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384"
        ]
        rng.shuffle(tokens)
        cipher = b":".join(tokens[:_bounded(rng.randint(1, 6), 1, 6)])

    # Prepare file entries
    entries: List[tuple[bytes, bytes]] = []
    entries.append((FILENAMES[0], peer_cert))
    entries.append((FILENAMES[1], local_cert_chain))
    if provide_key:
        entries.append((FILENAMES[2], private_key))

    # Serialize buffer
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    parts.append(b"TLSG")
    parts.append(struct.pack("<B", count))

    for name, content in entries:
        name = name[:255]
        max_len = 1500
        content = content[:max_len]
        parts.append(struct.pack("<B", len(name)))
        parts.append(name)
        parts.append(struct.pack("<H", len(content)))
        parts.append(content)

    # Parameters
    parts.append(struct.pack("<I", chooser))
    for v in flags:
        parts.append(struct.pack("<I", v))

    clen = min(len(cipher), 1024)
    parts.append(struct.pack("<H", clen))
    parts.append(cipher[:clen])

    blob = b"".join(parts)

    # Ensure size constraint
    return blob[:4096]
